visual_anchor: MRI linguine sign of collapsed implant shell; US snowstorm from extracapsular silicone.
rationale: Distinct implant complication with memorable cross-modality signs and possible palpable silicone/adenopathy.

visual_anchor: Rapidly enlarging mobile mass; mammographic oval mass/developing asymmetry and parallel hypoechoic US mass.
rationale: Standalone mass-forming benign stromal lesion and carcinoma mimic; imaging is nonspecific but clinical and radiologic pattern is useful.

visual_anchor: Pregnancy/lactation-associated mobile mass; US circumscribed oval lesion, becoming complex/cystic if infarcted.
rationale: Distinct pregnancy-associated mass; useful clinical/imaging differential from galactocele and fibroadenoma.

canonical_name: Granular Cell Tumor of the Breast
visual_anchor: Firm superficial mass with skin/nipple retraction; spiculated mammographic mass and posterior shadowing on US.
rationale: High-value carcinoma mimic with visible and radiologic manifestations; diagnosis is confirmed histologically.
source_heading: Granular Cell Tumor of the Breast
final_name: Granular Cell Tumor of the Breast

visual_anchor: Retroareolar cystic-solid lesion with mural nodule and possible bloody discharge.
rationale: Bundled encapsulated, solid, and invasive papillary carcinomas are biologically distinct; described imaging pattern overlaps intraductal papilloma and does not support one coherent standalone topic.

visual_anchor: Chronic breast mass with skin sinus; US shows heterogeneous collection and fistulous tract, sometimes necrotic axillary nodes.
rationale: Distinct chronic infection that mimics carcinoma and has a teachable sinus/abscess pattern.

visual_anchor: Adolescent/young adult with localized firm mass; ultrasound clustered cysts of varying size (“Swiss cheese”).
rationale: Named age-specific lesion with a recognizable ultrasound pattern, distinct from solitary papilloma and juvenile fibroadenoma.

visual_anchor: Mammographic grouped calcifications, architectural distortion, or mass.
rationale: Common imaging findings are nonspecific and the teaching value is mainly histopathologic; current radial-scar topic is a neighboring benign mimic, but not the same disease.

visual_anchor: Years after breast irradiation, violaceous bruise-like plaques/nodules in field; skin thickening or enhancing cutaneous mass.
rationale: Distinct secondary cutaneous angiosarcoma phenotype; keep separate from primary parenchymal breast angiosarcoma.

visual_anchor: Constricted breast base, high fold, enlarged areola, and glandular herniation producing a tubular/Snoopy contour.
rationale: Congenital visible deformity diagnosed by inspection, with a specific contour not represented by Poland syndrome.

visual_anchor: Unilateral erythematous, warm, tender neonatal breast bud; US fluid collection if abscess.
rationale: Distinct neonatal infection and recognizable age/site presentation; not physiologic bilateral hormonal enlargement or lactational mastitis.

visual_anchor: Rapid superficial masses, often multiple/bilateral round circumscribed lesions without spiculation.
rationale: This is a heterogeneous secondary-deposit category without a single disease-specific appearance; melanoma, lymphoma, and primary tumors already have separate records.

canonical_name: Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma of the Breast
visual_anchor: Slow central/periareolar mass, sometimes painful; imaging may be circumscribed or irregular.
rationale: Rare histologic carcinoma subtype with no reliable characteristic image or clinical anchor beyond a nonspecific mass.
source_heading: Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma of the Breast
final_name: Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma of the Breast

visual_anchor: Circumscribed mobile breast mass in a child, adolescent, or young adult; oval hypoechoic US lesion.
rationale: Age is notable but imaging overlaps common benign masses and diagnosis rests on histology; inadequate independent visual signature.

visual_anchor: Irregular/spiculated mass and abnormal axillary nodes.
rationale: A special histologic subtype with nonspecific imaging; nodal disease is not unique enough to justify a separate visual topic.

visual_anchor: Slow, painless mobile breast mass, often in older man or postmenopausal woman; circumscribed oval lesion.
rationale: The proposed circumscribed breast mass overlaps common benign tumors; definitive separation is histologic and adds limited independent visual teaching value.

visual_anchor: Screen-detected grouped amorphous, pleomorphic, or fine-linear calcifications.
rationale: High-risk precursor is established by histology and calcifications are nonspecific; overlap with existing DCIS topic without a separate visual disease signature.

visual_anchor: Irregular mass, asymmetry, or calcifications.
rationale: Imaging is nonspecific and the central distinction is histologic (myoepithelial layer); a pathology-led entity rather than a visual atlas topic.

visual_anchor: Older woman with circumscribed central mass, occasionally complex cystic-solid.
rationale: Named biphasic pathology with nonspecific imaging and no stable disease-specific clinical appearance.

canonical_name: Atypical Vascular Lesion of the Irradiated Breast
visual_anchor: Small pink/brown or erythematous papules/vesicles arising in irradiated breast skin.
rationale: Visible post-radiation skin lesion is an important differential of radiation-associated angiosarcoma; retain separately because benign atypical vascular lesion is not angiosarcoma.
source_heading: Atypical Vascular Lesion of the Irradiated Breast
final_name: Atypical Vascular Lesion of the Irradiated Breast

visual_anchor: Grouped coarse/pleomorphic calcifications or complex cystic mass.
rationale: Calcifications/cystic mass are nonspecific and the lesion is principally a histologic risk-stratification diagnosis.

canonical_name: Hyperkeratosis of the Nipple and Areola
visual_anchor: Verrucous brown hyperkeratosis involving nipple and areola, unilateral or bilateral.
rationale: Directly photographable skin/nipple diagnosis with no imaging requirement; distinct from Paget disease.
source_heading: Hyperkeratosis of the Nipple and Areola
final_name: Hyperkeratosis of the Nipple and Areola

visual_anchor: Firm subareolar mass with nipple inversion/retraction or enlargement; irregular subareolar lesion.
rationale: Rare locally infiltrative nipple tumor but imaging and examination overlap nipple adenoma and carcinoma; limited standalone visual specificity.

visual_anchor: Isolated breast budding before age 8 without other pubertal signs.
rationale: Developmental normal-variant presentation rather than a distinct lesion suitable for an atlas disease topic.

visual_anchor: Congenital absence of breast mound (amastia) or gland with preserved nipple-areola (amazia); pectoralis present.
rationale: Distinct visible congenital phenotype and clinically useful distinction from Poland syndrome and accessory breast tissue.

visual_anchor: Firm, high, spherical, distorted breast after implant placement; Baker III visible distortion, IV pain/hardness.
rationale: Standalone visible implant complication; no current broad implant topic and distinct from rupture.

visual_anchor: CT urography shows enhancing filling defect or urothelial thickening in renal pelvis/ureter; ureteroscopy shows papillary tumor.
rationale: Distinct upper-tract primary site from existing bladder urothelial carcinoma; radiologic localization is central.

visual_anchor: Multiphase contrast CT grades laceration/vascular injury; delayed phase demonstrates urinary extravasation and perirenal hematoma.
rationale: Acute trauma entity with management-driving, image-based grading and no existing renal injury topic.

visual_anchor: Retrograde CT cystogram shows extraperitoneal perivesical/Retzius leak or intraperitoneal contrast outlining bowel.
rationale: High-yield trauma pattern with distinct imaging and management implications.

visual_anchor: Retrograde urethrogram shows contrast extravasation at membranous urethra after pelvic fracture or bulbar urethra after straddle injury.
rationale: Distinct urethral trauma site patterns, often accompanied by recognizable perineal/butterfly hematoma; no existing topic.

visual_anchor: Plain film may show a spiculated “jackstone” in bladder; confirm at cystoscopy.
rationale: A discrete visible stone morphology and endoscopic finding; distinct from upper-tract nephrolithiasis.

visual_anchor: Voiding/cystographic study shows intravesical cobra-head ureterocele; duplex obstruction may produce drooping-lily sign.
rationale: Congenital urinary anomaly with recognizable imaging signs and potential visible prolapse; not covered by reflux or megaureter topics.

visual_anchor: MR urography depicts ureter inserting distal to sphincter; continuous incontinence despite normal voiding in a girl.
rationale: Anatomic anomaly with a classic clinical clue and imaging confirmation; separate from ectopic testis/cryptorchidism.

visual_anchor: VCUG shows dilated anterior urethra proximal to valve, sometimes with anterior urethral diverticulum.
rationale: Distinct anterior obstruction pattern; existing posterior urethral valves do not subsume it.

visual_anchor: Small intratesticular avascular mass with concentric onion-ring/lamellated ultrasound echoes.
rationale: Highly recognizable benign testicular lesion that can mimic malignancy and alter operative decision-making.

visual_anchor: Fever/dysuria with rim-enhancing intraprostatic fluid collection on TRUS, CT, or MRI.
rationale: Distinct focal suppurative complication with characteristic drainable collection, not covered by BPH or prostatitis-spectrum topics.

visual_anchor: MRI/CT triad: unilateral renal agenesis, ipsilateral seminal-vesicle cyst, and ejaculatory-duct obstruction.
rationale: Compact congenital syndrome with a specific cross-sectional imaging triad and clinically useful pelvic-mass differential.

visual_anchor: Normal corporal length concealed by suprapubic/scrotal skin, visible as a buried shaft; stretched length is normal.
rationale: Distinct visible genital anomaly and bedside distinction from micropenis; no existing topic.

visual_anchor: A constricting hair or thread with distal swelling or ischemia on a digit, toe, or penis; include genital presentations within one topic.
rationale: Urgent, visually recognizable strangulation syndrome with a clear physical finding and no current parent topic.

visual_anchor: Acute scrotal wall edema/hyperemia with normal testes and epididymides; transverse Doppler “fountain” pattern.
rationale: Important benign acute-scrotum mimic with a distinct sonographic sign and potential to avoid exploration.

visual_anchor: Right ureter courses behind IVC with reverse-J/fishhook or S-shaped course on urography.
rationale: Congenital anatomic obstruction with distinctive cross-sectional/urographic course, separate from UPJ obstruction.

visual_anchor: CT shows thin/mural calcified plaques coating bladder or collecting-system urothelium, often with alkaline urine.
rationale: Specific encrusting infectious pattern distinct from emphysematous cystitis, which shows gas.

visual_anchor: Young adult with frequency/pain and a contracted thick-walled small bladder on imaging/cystoscopy.
rationale: Imaging appearance is explicitly nonspecific and overlaps existing interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome; substance exposure alone does not supply a distinct visual anchor.

visual_anchor: Urethrogram shows ventral bulbar channel/filling defect; MRI/US localizes dilated Cowper duct.
rationale: Distinct male urethral gland duct lesion with a demonstrable imaging pattern, not covered by nonspecific stricture.

visual_anchor: VCUG demonstrates paraureteral bladder outpouching near ureteral orifice, often associated with reflux.
rationale: Congenital diverticulum is distinct from urachal anomalies and patent urachus; imaging-defined wall outpouching merits its own entry.

visual_anchor: Imaging shows markedly enlarged smooth bladder with bilateral megaureters/reflux and no urethral obstruction.
rationale: Distinct congenital bladder/ureter phenotype; not primary obstructive megaureter or megacystis-microcolon-intestinal hypoperistalsis syndrome.

visual_anchor: Phenotypic male with uterus/tubes on pelvic imaging, often discovered during hernia/cryptorchidism surgery.
rationale: Distinct developmental syndrome with striking cross-sectional/surgical anatomy and clinical exam relevance.

visual_anchor: Painful palpable dorsal penile cord; Doppler shows thrombosed superficial dorsal vein with absent flow.
rationale: Distinct venous thrombosis with confirmatory Doppler and cord appearance; do not merge with lymphangitis.

visual_anchor: Firm mobile serpiginous cord encircles or lies just proximal to coronal sulcus, usually without dorsal vein thrombosis.
rationale: Separate lymphatic process from Mondor superficial thrombophlebitis; the clinical differential itself is visually teachable.

visual_anchor: Deforming penile nodules, induration, ulcers, or draining sinuses after injection of paraffin/oil.
rationale: Distinct injection-related foreign-body disease with visible deformity and skin breakdown; no existing penile malignancy topic captures it.

visual_anchor: Small midline ventral penile/perineal cyst along median raphe, apparent at birth or later.
rationale: Visible congenital cutaneous cyst with specific midline anatomy and no existing equivalent.

visual_anchor: Small solid intratesticular mass; precocious puberty or gynecomastia may accompany hormone secretion.
rationale: US is nonspecific and definitive recognition is histologic; existing germ-cell tumor is broad enough for initial mass workup absent a distinctive visual signature.

visual_anchor: Acute pain with wedge-shaped avascular intratesticular segment and preserved flow in remainder.
rationale: Strong imaging discriminator from torsion and tumor; distinct focal infarction pattern.

visual_anchor: Scrotal skin extends onto ventral shaft and erases penoscrotal angle, often apparent with erection/traction.
rationale: Distinct congenital external phenotype with direct clinical photograph teaching value.

visual_anchor: Scrotum lies cranial to penis, partially or completely; photograph defines degree of transposition.
rationale: Distinct congenital external genital anomaly with clear visual recognition and surgical relevance.

visual_anchor: Persistent penile bend with orthotopic meatus, typically evident with erection; curvature documented by erection photograph.
rationale: Distinct congenital penile shape abnormality; keep separate from acquired Peyronie plaque/curvature.

visual_anchor: Newborn interlabial cyst displaces urethral meatus off midline; US shows paraurethral cyst.
rationale: Characteristic neonatal external finding with obstruction differential and no existing urethral topic.

visual_anchor: Penis balloons during voiding; VCUG shows markedly dilated urethra without distal valve.
rationale: Rare but striking congenital urethral morphology; differs from valve obstruction and stricture.

visual_anchor: Two urethral openings/channels demonstrated on exam and VCUG/retrograde urethrogram.
rationale: Distinct anatomic anomaly with visible clinical clue and direct radiographic demonstration.

visual_anchor: CT shows abundant pelvic fat compressing bladder into an inverted-teardrop shape, often with upper-tract obstruction.
rationale: Distinct imaging-defined pelvic disease, not generic hydronephrosis or obesity.

visual_anchor: Urography shows multiple small smooth round filling defects in renal pelvis/ureter from mucosal cysts.
rationale: Characteristic multifocal urothelial filling-defect pattern distinct from urothelial carcinoma and stones.

visual_anchor: Midline cyst along urachal tract between bladder dome and umbilicus.
rationale: Urachal carcinoma catalog record explicitly includes congenital urachal anomalies; this is a named subtype within that existing combined entry.

visual_anchor: Gross hematuria with serpiginous/corkscrew suburothelial vessels; angiography shows cirsoid AVM nidus.
rationale: Distinct vascular cause of hematuria with angiographic vascular morphology and no existing renal AVM topic.

visual_anchor: Prepubertal boy with focal hyperechoic scrotal fat adjacent to normal testes, sometimes following cold exposure.
rationale: Distinct benign extratesticular acute-scrotum mimic with ultrasound localization that separates it from torsion.

canonical_name: Fibrous pseudotumor of the tunica vaginalis
visual_anchor: Scrotal US shows multiple solid extratesticular tunical nodules, often T2-dark on MRI, with testis spared.
rationale: Distinct benign paratesticular fibrous pseudotumor and useful testis-sparing imaging differential.
source_heading: Fibrous pseudotumor of the tunica vaginalis
final_name: Fibrous pseudotumor of the tunica vaginalis

visual_anchor: Color Doppler left-to-right jet across the ventricular septum; a large shunt enlarges the left atrium and ventricle.
rationale: Distinct congenital shunt with a teachable Doppler jet; the listed AV septal defect is an inlet lesion with different anatomy.

visual_anchor: Interatrial communication with Doppler shunting and right sided volume loading; show secundum and sinus venosus anatomy and label associated anomalous pulmonary veins.
rationale: Common atrial shunt with a clear echo target and a different site from the existing complete AV septal defect.

visual_anchor: Ductal color jet from descending aorta to left pulmonary artery; large PDA produces left-heart enlargement and pulmonary plethora.
rationale: Distinct arterial shunt and ductal-view Doppler sign; not the existing aortopulmonary window.

visual_anchor: Doming pulmonary valve with turbulent systolic flow and poststenotic main pulmonary artery dilation.
rationale: Distinct valve-level lesion with reproducible echo and radiographic findings; Noonan syndrome is not a substitute for the lesion.

visual_anchor: Restricted aortic leaflet opening with Doppler flow acceleration; include calcific adult stenosis and congenital valve morphology as clearly labeled forms.
rationale: Create one aortic stenosis page covering degenerative calcific and congenital valvar forms with clear age-specific valve morphology and imaging. The existing rheumatic heart disease and bicuspid aortopathy pages do not provide a general stenosis overview.

visual_anchor: Systolic billowing or flail mitral scallop above the annular plane with eccentric regurgitant jet on 2D/3D echo.
rationale: A named valve phenotype with strong echo teaching value; distinct from rheumatic mitral stenosis and its fused commissures.

visual_anchor: Circumferential apical or midventricular ballooning with basal hyperkinesis on echo or ventriculography.
rationale: Recognizable imaging pattern and important ACS mimic; separate from apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

visual_anchor: Apical hypertrophy and spade-shaped left ventricular cavity on MRI or ventriculography.
rationale: Apical morphology and giant negative T waves are already explicitly covered in the existing hypertrophic cardiomyopathy topic; add this as a dedicated phenotype section there rather than a separate disease page.

visual_anchor: Prominent apical/lateral trabeculations with deep perfused recesses and thin compact myocardium on echo or CMR.
rationale: Left ventricular hypertrabeculation is a morphologic trait rather than a distinct cardiomyopathy in the 2023 ESC framework. Avoid presenting physiologic trabeculation as a disease; teach the pattern within its clinical cardiomyopathy context.

visual_anchor: Small independently mobile, stalked valvular mass with a fronded/shimmering edge on echocardiography.
rationale: The valve-based mass and embolic presentation are visually distinct from the listed atrial myxoma.

visual_anchor: Angiographic intimal flap/double lumen or long smooth narrowing from intramural hematoma in a coronary artery.
rationale: Distinct nonatherosclerotic coronary emergency with characteristic angiographic patterns; no existing coronary dissection topic.

canonical_name: Anomalous Aortic Origin of a Coronary Artery
visual_anchor: Coronary CTA shows an anomalous ostium from the opposite sinus, slit-like takeoff, and interarterial/intramural course.
rationale: High-value coronary CTA anatomy distinct from the listed anomalous coronary origin from the pulmonary artery.
source_heading: Anomalous Aortic Origin of a Coronary Artery
final_name: Anomalous Aortic Origin of a Coronary Artery

visual_anchor: A windsock sac arising from a sinus of Valsalva into a chamber, with a jet if ruptured.
rationale: A named root lesion with a characteristic echo/CTA morphology distinct from fusiform thoracic aneurysm.

visual_anchor: Dilated tortuous coronary artery traced on CTA/angiography to a cardiac chamber or pulmonary artery, with Doppler runoff.
rationale: Distinct coronary runoff anatomy and Doppler finding; not the existing pulmonary-origin coronary anomaly.

canonical_name: Congenitally Corrected Transposition of the Great Arteries
visual_anchor: Echo/CMR demonstrates both atrioventricular and ventriculoarterial discordance; anterior-left aorta and systemic morphologic RV.
rationale: A separate double-discordance anatomy with distinct lifelong imaging; D-TGA has concordant AV connections.
source_heading: Congenitally Corrected Transposition of the Great Arteries
final_name: Congenitally Corrected Transposition of the Great Arteries

visual_anchor: CTA/MRA or angiography shows multifocal string-of-beads stenoses, especially in renal or cervical arteries.
rationale: Distinct nonatherosclerotic arteriopathy with signature vascular imaging and important SCAD association.

visual_anchor: Noncontrast CT shows crescentic high attenuation in aortic wall; contrast CT shows thickening without an intimal flap.
rationale: The existing Acute Aortic Dissection topic already lists intramural hematoma among CTA manifestations. Expand that parent with the noncontrast crescentic hyperattenuation and no-flap distinction rather than creating a second page.

visual_anchor: CTA shows a focal contrast-filled crater penetrating aortic plaque, often with adjacent intramural hematoma.
rationale: Different acute aortic syndrome morphology from dissection and fusiform aneurysm; characteristic CTA finding.

visual_anchor: CT/CMR maps anomalous pulmonary veins draining to systemic venous structures; sinus venosus defects may coexist while the fossa ovalis remains intact.
rationale: The sinus venosus ASD component belongs with the new ASD topic. PAPVR merits a distinct page for anomalous venous drainage and right-heart volume loading; the catalog has total anomalous return and scimitar syndrome but not partial anomalous return.
source_heading: Sinus Venosus Atrial Septal Defect and Partial Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Return

canonical_name: Pulmonary Atresia with Ventricular Septal Defect
visual_anchor: CTA maps atretic RV outflow, VSD/overriding aorta, and major aortopulmonary collateral arteries supplying lung segments.
rationale: Distinct cyanotic anatomy and collateral map; existing intact-septum pulmonary atresia and TOF do not capture this configuration.
source_heading: Pulmonary Atresia with Ventricular Septal Defect
final_name: Pulmonary Atresia with Ventricular Septal Defect

visual_anchor: CTA/3D reconstruction shows complete interruption of the arch with descending aorta supplied through the duct.
rationale: Complete arch discontinuity is visually distinct from listed coarctation, a focal narrowing.

visual_anchor: Echo/CMR shows both great arteries arising predominantly from the right ventricle and defines VSD-to-outlet relationship.
rationale: Distinct conotruncal anatomy whose VSD relationship determines physiology; does not duplicate listed TGA or truncus.

visual_anchor: Cross-sectional imaging shows abnormal organ situs, systemic/pulmonary venous return, and cardiac position/segmental anatomy.
rationale: Distinctive multisystem laterality pattern with highly visual cardiac and visceral anatomy; no existing heterotaxy topic.

visual_anchor: Echo shows a discrete fibrous/fibromuscular shelf below an normally opening aortic valve with LVOT jet.
rationale: A discrete membrane is distinct from muscle-mediated obstructive HCM and valvar aortic stenosis.

visual_anchor: Echo depicts multilevel left-sided obstruction: parachute mitral valve/ring, subaortic ridge, and coarctation.
rationale: A recognizable combined congenital pattern rather than a redundant isolated lesion; existing coarctation covers only one level.

visual_anchor: Left atrial membrane separates pulmonary venous chamber from distal atrium; appendage lies distal to the membrane.
rationale: Distinct membrane anatomy and Doppler gradient; clarifies difference from supravalvar mitral ring.

canonical_name: Right Aortic Arch with Aberrant Left Subclavian Artery
visual_anchor: CTA shows right arch and aberrant left subclavian from Kommerell diverticulum; esophagram may show posterior indentation.
rationale: Distinct vascular ring configuration with a characteristic CT course; existing double arch is a different ring.
source_heading: Right Aortic Arch with Aberrant Left Subclavian Artery
final_name: Right Aortic Arch with Aberrant Left Subclavian Artery

visual_anchor: CTA shows left pulmonary artery arising from right pulmonary artery and passing between trachea and esophagus.
rationale: Rare but high-yield airway-compression configuration, distinct from aortic vascular rings.

visual_anchor: Echo/CMR shows anomalous muscle bundle dividing RV into high-pressure inlet and low-pressure outlet, with normal pulmonary valve.
rationale: Distinct intracavitary obstruction and echo finding, unlike valvar pulmonary stenosis.

visual_anchor: Aneurysmal pulmonary arteries and rudimentary valve with severe stenosis/regurgitation compress adjacent bronchi on CT.
rationale: Absent pulmonary valve is a recognizable tetralogy variant already accommodated by the existing Tetralogy of Fallot topic, which includes pulmonary artery tree imaging and airway compression. Add the aneurysmal pulmonary artery/bronchial compression pattern as a variant subsection.

visual_anchor: Echo shows domed unicuspid/bicuspid congenital valve with high gradient, sometimes duct-dependent systemic flow in neonate.
rationale: Fold congenital and calcific causes into one new Aortic Stenosis page (candidate 31), with age/valve morphology as separate etiologies. This is a closely related valve lesion and avoids proliferating separate pages for the same stenosis syndrome.

visual_anchor: CTA shows isthmic intimal injury, pseudoaneurysm or contour defect with periaortic/mediastinal hematoma after deceleration trauma.
rationale: Mechanism, location, and acute imaging differ from spontaneous aortic dissection; a distinct trauma diagnosis.

visual_anchor: CTA shows rapidly enlarging saccular aneurysm with periaortic inflammatory stranding/fluid or gas.
rationale: Infection changes the characteristic morphology and urgency; distinct from listed degenerative aneurysm topics.

visual_anchor: CTA/MRA shows long mid-thoracic/abdominal aortic narrowing with renal/visceral branch stenoses and collaterals.
rationale: Anatomic distribution and branch involvement distinguish it from isthmic coarctation.

visual_anchor: Dynamic duplex/MRA shows popliteal artery compression with plantar flexion and abnormal gastrocnemius relationship.
rationale: Distinct dynamic compression syndrome in young athletes, unlike atherosclerotic peripheral arterial disease.

visual_anchor: Ultrasound/MRI shows nonenhancing mucin cysts in popliteal arterial adventitia causing smooth eccentric/scimitar narrowing.
rationale: A rare but iconic vessel-wall cyst with a clear imaging sign, distinct from muscular entrapment.

visual_anchor: Angiography shows ulnar artery aneurysm/occlusion over the hook of hamate with distal digital emboli.
rationale: Specific occupational arterial injury with distinctive angiographic site and hand findings; no existing comparator.

visual_anchor: Left renal vein compression with a beak and gonadal or pelvic collaterals on Doppler or CT, paired with compatible hematuria or pain; distinguish asymptomatic compression.
rationale: Distinct venous compression syndrome with a recognizable cross-sectional sign; May-Thurner is a different vessel.

visual_anchor: Contrast CT/venography shows SVC narrowing or occlusion and azygos/chest-wall collateral pathways; facial plethora is visible clinically.
rationale: Clinically and radiologically recognizable syndrome spanning many causes; neither malignant causes nor venous thrombosis topics substitute for the obstruction pattern.

visual_anchor: CTA with arm elevation shows subclavian artery compression, often poststenotic aneurysm and distal emboli; radiograph may show cervical rib.
rationale: Distinct arterial compression and embolic phenotype, unlike listed effort venous thrombosis.

visual_anchor: Cardiac MRI may show edema and noncoronary enhancement, but these findings do not distinguish giant-cell myocarditis.
rationale: The defining giant-cell finding requires myocardial biopsy; candidate has no distinctive clinical or radiologic anchor beyond nonspecific myocarditis findings, so it fails the visual-manifestation criterion.

visual_anchor: CMR shows myocardial edema with subepicardial or mid-wall nonischemic enhancement, often lateral, not following a coronary territory.
rationale: The MRI pattern is useful for acute myocarditis but cannot establish a lymphocytic histotype. Use one acute myocarditis page that teaches CMR edema and nonischemic enhancement, with biopsy subtypes in the differential.

visual_anchor: Echo shows transient ventricular dysfunction with possible coronary dilation/aneurysm and pericardial effusion after postinfectious illness.
rationale: Distinct shock-predominant postinfectious pediatric syndrome with an echo anchor; Kawasaki disease remains a separate syndrome.

visual_anchor: TEE shows broad-based small valve vegetations without leaflet destruction or abscess, in a patient with systemic emboli.
rationale: Sterile thrombotic vegetations have a distinct clinical context and imaging contrast with destructive infective endocarditis.

visual_anchor: Plain films/CT show extensive arterial-wall calcification in an infant, often involving aorta and coronary arteries.
rationale: Rare disease with a highly distinctive age-specific radiographic pattern, unlike valve calcification of older adults.

visual_anchor: Peripheral discontinuous nodular enhancement with progressive centripetal fill-in; markedly T2-bright liver lesion.
rationale: Common benign liver mass with a highly recognizable imaging pattern; distinct from FNH and adenoma.

visual_anchor: Homogeneous arterial hyperenhancement with a central T2-bright scar and delayed scar enhancement.
rationale: Distinctive benign liver lesion and useful imaging differential from adenoma and hemangioma.

visual_anchor: Arterially enhancing liver mass; subtype clues include opposed-phase signal drop (HNF1A) or inflammatory atoll sign.
rationale: Distinct tumor with clinically important hemorrhage/malignant potential and useful MRI subtype patterns.

visual_anchor: Gallbladder wall thickening with intramural Rokitansky–Aschoff sinuses producing ultrasound comet-tail artifact or MRI pearl-necklace sign.
rationale: Strong modality-specific pattern and gallbladder carcinoma mimic.

visual_anchor: Curvilinear or patchy calcification conforming to the gallbladder wall on CT.
rationale: Use a porcelain-gallbladder subsection in the existing gallstones/cholecystitis topic: it is an imaging phenotype in the same organ disease page, and wall calcification is its visual anchor.

visual_anchor: Gas outlining or within the gallbladder wall, sometimes extending into the lumen or pericholecystic tissues on CT.
rationale: Use an emphysematous-cholecystitis subsection in the existing gallstones/cholecystitis topic. Intramural gas is a distinct emergency pattern, but it remains a cholecystitis subtype within the same gallbladder disease page.

visual_anchor: Microcystic honeycomb pancreatic mass with central scar or sunburst calcification and no duct communication.
rationale: Classic appearance distinct from IPMN and mucinous cystic neoplasm.

visual_anchor: Body/tail multilocular cystic pancreatic mass in a woman, with septa or peripheral calcification and no duct communication.
rationale: Distinct cystic neoplasm with malignant potential and useful contrast to serous neoplasm/IPMN.

visual_anchor: Well-circumscribed encapsulated pancreatic mass with hemorrhagic/cystic center and peripheral solid tissue.
rationale: Characteristic young-patient tumor pattern, distinct from ductal adenocarcinoma and other cysts.

visual_anchor: Endoscopic ulcerated or polypoid ampulla; CT/MRCP may show bile and pancreatic duct dilation ending at the ampulla.
rationale: Distinct anatomic primary with direct endoscopic teaching value.

visual_anchor: Small ovoid fat-attenuation lesion abutting colon with hyperattenuating rim and possible central dot on CT.
rationale: Classic CT diagnosis that prevents confusion with diverticulitis/appendicitis.

visual_anchor: Larger heterogeneous inflamed fat-density lesion within omentum, usually not directly abutting colon, without central dot.
rationale: Visually distinguishable benign acute-abdomen mimic; retain as distinct from epiploic appendagitis.

visual_anchor: Rigler pattern: ectopic gallstone, pneumobilia, and bowel obstruction; duodenal impaction in Bouveret syndrome.
rationale: High-yield emergency imaging pattern; Bouveret is a proximal presentation within the same disease spectrum.

visual_anchor: Abnormally rotated or upside-down stomach on radiograph/CT; mesenteroaxial form places antrum above gastroesophageal junction.
rationale: Distinct acute obstruction with characteristic anatomy; not redundant with paraesophageal hernia.

visual_anchor: CT sagittal narrowing of third duodenum between aorta and SMA with proximal gastric/duodenal dilation and reduced aortomesenteric angle/distance.
rationale: Anatomic cause of obstruction with a distinctive cross-sectional pattern.

visual_anchor: Fecaloma with colonic dilation and wall thickening plus pericolonic fat stranding, often rectosigmoid, on CT.
rationale: Important pressure-necrosis emergency with distinct imaging anchor.

visual_anchor: Thin circumferential mucosal ring at the distal esophagus, best seen as a short shelf-like narrowing on barium esophagram.
rationale: Classic structural cause of intermittent solid-food dysphagia; separate from peptic stricture.

visual_anchor: Multiple small, sharply demarcated punched-out esophageal ulcers on endoscopy, often distal; biopsy from ulcer edge.
rationale: Recognizable viral endoscopic pattern distinct from Candida plaques and CMV linear ulcers.

visual_anchor: Discrete opposing mid-esophageal ulcers at a pill-stasis site, often with focal mucosal injury on endoscopy.
rationale: Common iatrogenic mucosal injury with imageable focal endoscopic findings; distinct from caustic injury.

visual_anchor: Gastric folds/nodularity, shallow ulcers, or mass-like mucosal lesions on endoscopy; appearances can be patchy and nonspecific.
rationale: The existing conjunctival lymphoma topic already explicitly lists MALT lymphoma. Broaden and reorganize it as extranodal MALT lymphoma with gastric and ocular sections, preserving any other ocular lymphoma types separately.

visual_anchor: Liver biopsy may show interface hepatitis with lymphoplasmacytic portal infiltrates and hepatocyte rosettes.
rationale: The strongest image is histology/stool microscopy, and endoscopic mucosal changes are nonspecific; defer from this clinical/radiologic atlas scope.

visual_anchor: Root-of-mesentery misty fat or mass that encases mesenteric vessels while preserving a fat-ring halo; possible pseudocapsule on CT.
rationale: Distinct radiologic pattern and separate from encapsulating peritonitis.

visual_anchor: Fluid-filled, dilated tubular appendix with mural calcification or layered “onion-skin” appearance on ultrasound.
rationale: Use canonical topic “Appendiceal Mucocele”; mucocele is a descriptive gross/imaging term, while LAMN is a specific histologic neoplasm. Strong imaging anchor and not the same as disseminated pseudomyxoma.
source_heading: Appendiceal Mucocele and Low-Grade Appendiceal Mucinous Neoplasm

visual_anchor: Duodenal biopsy showing pear-shaped trophozoites adherent to mucosal surface; stool antigen/organism detection supports diagnosis.
rationale: The strongest image is histology/stool microscopy, and endoscopic mucosal changes are nonspecific; defer from this clinical/radiologic atlas scope.

visual_anchor: Pancreatic tissue encircling the second duodenum with proximal gastric/duodenal dilation on CT or upper GI contrast study.
rationale: Distinct congenital cause of duodenal obstruction, including adult presentations.

visual_anchor: Multiple dilated proximal small-bowel loops with abrupt atretic transition and gasless distal bowel on neonatal radiograph/contrast study.
rationale: Separate atresia level from duodenal atresia; valuable neonatal imaging topic.

visual_anchor: CT cluster of small-bowel loops in an abnormal sac/compartment with mesenteric vessel crowding or swirl; specify paraduodenal recess versus transmesenteric defect.
rationale: Internal hernias are a distinct cause of closed-loop obstruction; retain both sites under a combined topic.

visual_anchor: Encased clustered bowel loops within a thick fibrous peritoneal membrane (“abdominal cocoon”) on CT.
rationale: Distinct peritoneal process from mesenteric-root fibroinflammation; uncommon but highly visual.

visual_anchor: Respiratory dependent hooked proximal celiac artery narrowing on sagittal CTA or Doppler in a compatible symptomatic syndrome; isolated compression can be incidental.
rationale: Anatomically distinctive vascular compression pattern; retain as a separate syndrome from atherosclerotic ischemia.

visual_anchor: CTA shows severe ostial mesenteric arterial stenosis/occlusion with collateral vessels; chronic cases often have multivessel disease.
rationale: Clinically important chronic vascular disease distinct from already listed acute mesenteric ischemia.

visual_anchor: Portal, mesenteric, or splenic venous filling defects and chronic portal cavernous transformation; include infective pylephlebitis as a subtype.
rationale: Distinct venous thrombosis pattern vs hepatic venous obstruction in Budd–Chiari; grouped term is appropriate.

visual_anchor: Doppler ultrasound may show hepatomegaly, ascites, reduced/monophasic hepatic venous flow and portal-flow changes after transplant/chemotherapy.
rationale: Distinct sinusoidal microvascular injury versus large hepatic-vein thrombosis; visual imaging signs exist but are nonspecific.

canonical_name: Congestive Hepatopathy and Fontan-Associated Liver Disease
visual_anchor: Heterogeneous “nutmeg” liver enhancement, dilated hepatic veins/IVC and pulsatile portal flow on Doppler in right-sided heart failure/Fontan circulation.
rationale: Clinically useful congestive liver appearance distinct from thrombotic Budd–Chiari syndrome; combine Fontan-associated phenotype.
source_heading: Congestive Hepatopathy and Fontan-Associated Liver Disease
final_name: Congestive Hepatopathy and Fontan-Associated Liver Disease

visual_anchor: Sheet-like soft tissue in pancreaticoduodenal groove with medial duodenal wall thickening or cysts on MRI/CT.
rationale: Rare but recognizable pancreatitis pattern and important pancreatic cancer mimic.

visual_anchor: Diffuse peritoneal thickening/nodularity, omental cake, or ascites on CT, often without an identifiable gastrointestinal primary.
rationale: Distinct primary peritoneal malignancy and visual comparison with mucinous peritoneal disease.

visual_anchor: Small round acid-fast oocysts attached to the small-bowel epithelial brush border on stain; endoscopy may show villous blunting.
rationale: The strongest image is histology/stool microscopy, and endoscopic mucosal changes are nonspecific; defer from this clinical/radiologic atlas scope.

visual_anchor: Coin-shaped radiopaque object in esophagus on AP view; coins usually appear en face in esophagus, unlike airway orientation.
rationale: Directly imageable foreign-body emergency, distinct from battery injury.

visual_anchor: Two or more magnets in separate bowel loops or clumped across bowel walls on radiograph, with pressure injury/perforation risk.
rationale: Distinct and high-stakes imaging pattern compared with a single coin or button battery.

visual_anchor: Multiple peripheral hypoenhancing liver nodules coalescing to the capsule, with capsular retraction and possible “lollipop” vessel termination.
rationale: Distinct rare vascular malignancy with high-value imaging signature; not a hemangioma subtype.

visual_anchor: Numerous hepatic cysts with relative absence of renal cysts on CT/MRI.
rationale: Distinct from ADPKD-associated liver cysts and useful when symptomatic hepatomegaly occurs.

visual_anchor: Marked thickened gallbladder wall with intramural hypoattenuating nodules and stones on CT, often mimicking carcinoma.
rationale: Use a xanthogranulomatous-cholecystitis subsection in the existing gallstones/cholecystitis topic. It has a distinctive carcinoma-mimic pattern, but is an inflammatory cholecystitis subtype.

canonical_name: Secondary Sclerosing Cholangitis of Critical Illness
visual_anchor: MRCP/ERCP shows biliary casts, multifocal intrahepatic strictures and pruning after critical illness, initially sparing the extrahepatic duct.
rationale: Distinct ischemic cholangiopathy phenotype; not redundant with primary sclerosing cholangitis.
source_heading: Secondary Sclerosing Cholangitis of Critical Illness
final_name: Secondary Sclerosing Cholangitis of Critical Illness

visual_anchor: Multiloculated hepatic cyst with septa or mural nodules, usually no bile-duct communication; often in middle-aged women.
rationale: Distinct cystic neoplasm of liver from isolated polycystic disease and echinococcosis; retain as a separate site from pancreatic MCN.

visual_anchor: Coarse dark pigment in centrilobular hepatocytes and grossly black liver.
rationale: The defining visual feature is gross/histopathology and the syndrome otherwise has no distinctive clinical or radiologic image; defer for current visual atlas scope.

canonical_name: Undifferentiated Embryonal Sarcoma of the Liver
visual_anchor: Large heterogeneous pediatric liver mass that appears cystic on CT but predominantly solid on ultrasound.
rationale: Unusual cross-modality discrepancy makes a memorable tumor pattern; distinct from hepatoblastoma and infant hamartoma.
source_heading: Undifferentiated Embryonal Sarcoma of the Liver
final_name: Undifferentiated Embryonal Sarcoma of the Liver

visual_anchor: Large multicystic infant liver mass with thin septa and intervening solid stromal tissue on ultrasound/CT.
rationale: Distinct benign infant tumor with characteristic cystic imaging and useful malignant differential.

visual_anchor: Herniation through the Spigelian fascia along the semilunar line on CT or dynamic ultrasound.
rationale: Both are uncommon abdominal-wall/pelvic hernias with distinctive anatomic CT locations; combined topic is acceptable if clearly separated.

visual_anchor: Bowel extending through the obturator canal between the obturator and pectineus muscles on pelvic CT.
rationale: Both are uncommon abdominal-wall/pelvic hernias with distinctive anatomic CT locations; combined topic is acceptable if clearly separated.

visual_anchor: Barium esophagram shows numerous tiny flask-shaped intramural outpouchings, sometimes with a stricture.
rationale: Rare but highly characteristic contrast-study appearance, distinct from true diverticula and candidal plaques.

visual_anchor: CT shows linear or bubbly gas within thickened gastric wall, possibly portal venous gas, with severe systemic illness.
rationale: High-stakes imaging emergency, distinguishable from benign gastric emphysema.

visual_anchor: Gross specimen with yellow flecks in red gallbladder mucosa (“strawberry gallbladder”); ultrasound may show fixed nonshadowing polyps.
rationale: Teaching anchor is predominantly gross pathology and ultrasound findings are nonspecific; lower value than actionable radiologic gallbladder entities.

visual_anchor: Cyst adjacent to bowel with layered inner echogenic mucosa and outer hypoechoic muscle (“gut signature”) on ultrasound.
rationale: Distinct congenital lesion with a strong sonographic sign, separate from Meckel diverticulum.

visual_anchor: Upper endoscopy shows adult hookworms attached to duodenal/jejunal mucosa, sometimes with punctate bleeding.
rationale: Direct parasite visualization supports a memorable visual topic; separate from skin manifestations of animal hookworm.

visual_anchor: Terminal ileal wall thickening and mesenteric lymphadenopathy on CT/ultrasound, with a relatively normal appendix in pseudoappendicitis.
rationale: Distinct infectious ileitis and helpful Crohn/appendicitis differential; the source text describes a typical pseudoappendicitis presentation with reactive arthritis/erythema nodosum as possible sequelae.

visual_anchor: Hypervascular pancreatic lesion on arterial CT/MRI or receptor PET in fasting hypoglycemia.
rationale: Distinct functioning pancreatic tumor with a strong localization anchor.

visual_anchor: Pancreatic tail mass and liver lesions with secretory diarrhea and hypokalemia.
rationale: Distinct hormone-secreting tumor syndrome.

visual_anchor: Generalized hyperpigmentation after bilateral adrenalectomy with enlarging pituitary macroadenoma on MRI.
rationale: Specific visible post-adrenalectomy syndrome.

visual_anchor: Sudden headache/ophthalmoplegia; MRI shows hemorrhagic or infarcted sellar mass.
rationale: Urgent image-defined pituitary emergency.

visual_anchor: Midline nonenhancing sellar cyst with intracystic T2-dark waxy nodule.
rationale: Useful imaging distinction from craniopharyngioma.

visual_anchor: Infantile-onset gigantism with pituitary hyperplasia.
rationale: Existing acromegaly topic includes pituitary gigantism; etiology adds no distinct visual pattern.

visual_anchor: Rugger-jersey spine, salt-and-pepper skull, and subperiosteal resorption in CKD.
rationale: Recognizable secondary hyperparathyroid bone pattern.

visual_anchor: Rachitic metaphyseal cupping/fraying with total alopecia.
rationale: Alopecia distinctly anchors this rickets phenotype.

visual_anchor: Rickets with cupping and fraying, hair preserved.
rationale: Radiographs overlap existing rickets topic; enzyme subtype has no distinct visual pattern.

visual_anchor: Childhood generalized bone expansion and long-bone deformity.
rationale: Juvenile phenotype differs visibly from adult Paget disease.

visual_anchor: Short stature with metaphyseal widening, cupping/fraying, and cortical erosion.
rationale: Distinctive metaphyseal skeletal dysplasia.

visual_anchor: Kenny-Caffey: deep-set eyes, cortical thickening, and medullary stenosis on long-bone films.
rationale: Split bundled syndromes because their skeletal patterns differ.

visual_anchor: Severe growth deficiency and characteristic face with deep set eyes, beaked nose, micrognathia, and congenital hypoparathyroidism; skeletal findings vary.
rationale: Distinct recognizable clinical phenotype; facial photographs and a cohort description support visual teaching. Do not distinguish from Kenny-Caffey by presumed absent medullary stenosis.

visual_anchor: Bilateral bulky nodular adrenals with Cushing phenotype.
rationale: Existing Cushing syndrome topic covers phenotype and adrenal imaging; this is a subtype.

visual_anchor: Craniosynostosis, bowed femora, atypical genitalia with adrenal steroidogenic failure.
rationale: Distinct congenital skeletal and sex-development phenotype.

visual_anchor: 46,XY phenotypic female infant with adrenal insufficiency and enlarged lipid-laden adrenals.
rationale: Steroidogenic subtype of congenital adrenal hyperplasia. Broaden the existing CAH page beyond 21 hydroxylase deficiency and retain cause specific phenotype labels.

visual_anchor: Hypertension, absent puberty, and undervirilization in 46,XY patient.
rationale: Steroidogenic subtype of congenital adrenal hyperplasia. Broaden the existing CAH page beyond 21 hydroxylase deficiency and retain cause specific phenotype labels.

visual_anchor: Adrenal crisis in infancy or later hypogonadism; adrenal cytomegaly is histologic.
rationale: Primarily biochemical/genetic recognition without a distinctive visual or radiologic anchor.

visual_anchor: Early obesity, adrenal insufficiency, and characteristic red hair.
rationale: Photographable phenotype differentiates this from common obesity.

visual_anchor: Multisystem childhood tumor-predisposition syndrome with goiter, pleuropulmonary blastoma, and ovarian tumor.
rationale: No single coherent visual anchor; component lesions have their own topics.

visual_anchor: Posterior mediastinal or adrenal mass, sometimes with secretory diarrhea.
rationale: Nonspecific mass appearance without a distinctive visual signature.

visual_anchor: Tall phenotypic female with streak gonads and 46,XY gonadal dysgenesis.
rationale: No distinctive external or imaging feature beyond broad DSD phenotype.

visual_anchor: 46,XY infant undervirilization with spontaneous virilization at puberty.
rationale: Distinct sex development disorder, but the proposed genital phenotype overlaps other steroidogenesis defects and supplies no separate radiologic discriminator.

visual_anchor: Maternal virilization, virilized 46,XX infant, and later multicystic ovaries.
rationale: Distinctive clinical and ovarian imaging phenotype.

visual_anchor: Early virilization with advanced bone age and suppressed LH.
rationale: Visual and radiographic findings overlap other precocious puberty causes.

visual_anchor: Phenotypic male with uterus and tubes on MRI or hernia surgery.
rationale: Specific anatomic syndrome; coordinate with duplicate Urology proposal.

visual_anchor: Postmenopausal virilization and bilateral ovarian stromal enlargement.
rationale: Clinical virilization is visible, but imaging overlaps androgen-producing tumors.

visual_anchor: Precocious puberty with delayed bone age, multicystic ovaries, and pituitary hyperplasia in severe hypothyroidism.
rationale: Distinct paradoxical puberty and imaging pattern.

visual_anchor: Partial lipodystrophy, Rieger anomaly, and characteristic triangular facies.
rationale: Photographable multisystem phenotype distinct from other lipodystrophies.

visual_anchor: Mandibular hypoplasia, deafness, and progeroid lipodystrophy.
rationale: MDPL is a distinct genetic disorder from mandibuloacral dysplasia; although both have progeroid/lipodystrophy features, this proposal does not provide enough independent visual value for a separate page. Do not merge the diseases.

visual_anchor: Congenital ichthyosis with Jordan anomaly (lipid vacuoles) in leukocytes.
rationale: Visible skin phenotype plus diagnostic smear finding.

visual_anchor: Postaxial polydactyly, bifid epiglottis, and hypothalamic hamartoma on MRI.
rationale: Distinct syndrome combines visible digit difference and airway/CNS findings.

visual_anchor: Neonatal progeroid facies, natal teeth, sparse hair, and lipoatrophy.
rationale: Distinct photographable neonatal phenotype.

visual_anchor: Facial plethora/chest-wall collaterals with bulky anterior mediastinal mass compressing SVC.
rationale: Recognizable mediastinal lymphoma distribution and presentation.

visual_anchor: Post-transplant extranodal allograft, GI, lung, skin, or CNS lesions on PET/CT.
rationale: Distinct post-transplant lymphoid disease with varied extranodal imaging.

visual_anchor: Fungating gingival/palatal mass with lytic maxillary or mandibular lesion.
rationale: Distinct oral tumor and bone imaging pattern.

visual_anchor: Large pleural, pericardial, or peritoneal effusion without mass or lymphadenopathy.
rationale: The proposed endoscopic or cross-sectional appearance is nonspecific and does not provide enough independent visual teaching value for a separate atlas entry.

canonical_name: Systemic ALK-positive anaplastic large cell lymphoma
visual_anchor: Ulcerated violaceous skin nodules with PET-avid nodal/visceral disease.
rationale: Systemic ALK-positive lymphoma is distinct from cutaneous and implant-associated ALCL.
source_heading: Systemic ALK-positive anaplastic large cell lymphoma
final_name: Systemic ALK-positive anaplastic large cell lymphoma

visual_anchor: Gastric thickened folds, nodules, shallow ulcers, or wall thickening.
rationale: The existing conjunctival lymphoma topic already explicitly lists MALT lymphoma. Broaden and reorganize it as extranodal MALT lymphoma with gastric and ocular sections, preserving any other ocular lymphoma types separately.

visual_anchor: Celiac-associated jejunal thickening and aneurysmal dilatation, with ulcers or perforation.
rationale: Distinct intestinal T-cell lymphoma pattern.

visual_anchor: Multifocal shallow small-bowel ulcers and strictures; CT wall thickening or duodenal mass.
rationale: A distinct intestinal lymphoma defined largely by histology and immunophenotype; the proposed ulcer and wall thickening images do not reliably distinguish it.

visual_anchor: Homogeneous hepatosplenomegaly without focal lesions or peripheral/retroperitoneal nodes.
rationale: The proposed endoscopic or cross-sectional appearance is nonspecific and does not provide enough independent visual teaching value for a separate atlas entry.

visual_anchor: Diffuse erythematous papules/plaques, periorbital edema, leonine facies.
rationale: Highly visible cutaneous leukemia phenotype.

visual_anchor: Single sharply edged oral or skin ulcer without mass or systemic lymphoma.
rationale: Distinct focal EBV ulcer presentation.

canonical_name: Immunoproliferative small intestinal disease (alpha heavy chain)
visual_anchor: Proximal small bowel thickened folds, cobblestoning, villous edema, and ulcers.
rationale: Distinctive endoscopic pattern and alpha-heavy-chain syndrome.
source_heading: Immunoproliferative small intestinal disease (alpha heavy chain)
final_name: Immunoproliferative small intestinal disease (alpha heavy chain)

visual_anchor: Spontaneous skin, muscle, or retroperitoneal hematomas without typical hemarthroses.
rationale: Distinct acquired factor inhibitor bleeding pattern from congenital hemophilia A.

visual_anchor: Delayed umbilical bleeding or neonatal intracranial hemorrhage despite normal PT/aPTT.
rationale: The supplied bleeding and intracranial hemorrhage appearances are nonspecific; diagnosis depends on coagulation testing rather than an independent visual phenotype.

visual_anchor: Wood-like conjunctival membranes and gingival pseudomembranes with tooth loss.
rationale: Directly visible ligneous disease phenotype.

visual_anchor: Noninflammatory retiform purpura, acral necrosis, and digital/ear gangrene.
rationale: Distinct occlusive disease from mixed cryoglobulinemic vasculitis.

visual_anchor: Facial/truncal telangiectasias plus perinephric fluid on CT/US and pulmonary shunt.
rationale: Distinct clinical-radiologic syndrome.

visual_anchor: Portal, mesenteric, or splenic venous filling defects and chronic portal cavernous transformation; include infective pylephlebitis as a subtype.
rationale: Different anatomy, complications, and MPN association from lower-limb DVT.

visual_anchor: Prenatal US: hydrops, scalp edema, ascites, cardiomegaly, and thick placenta.
rationale: Broaden the existing Alpha Thalassemia page beyond HbH disease and include the Hb Barts hydrops phenotype; do not create parallel genotype specific pages.

visual_anchor: Early severe gingivitis/periodontitis, oral ulcers, and alveolar bone loss.
rationale: Photographable oral disease and dental radiographic anchor.

visual_anchor: Blocked forearm rotation with bilateral proximal radioulnar synostosis and petechiae.
rationale: Distinct congenital skeletal-hematologic association; unlike TAR.

visual_anchor: Extensive refractory cutaneous/plantar/anogenital warts with recurrent infections.
rationale: Highly visible phenotype; related immunodeficiency topics lack this signature.

visual_anchor: Post-transplant Doppler: slow/reversed portal flow, gallbladder wall thickening, narrowed hepatic veins.
rationale: Distinct post-transplant hepatic vascular injury pattern.

visual_anchor: Hemorrhagic bullae, necrosis, and scars precisely at mosquito-bite sites.
rationale: Specific visible pattern distinct from hydroa vacciniforme-like LPD.

visual_anchor: Ulcerated plaques and subcutaneous tumors with FDG-avid skin nodules.
rationale: Overlaps existing subcutaneous panniculitis-like and cutaneous T-cell lymphoma records; separate visual value is not yet clear.

canonical_name: Primary cutaneous aggressive epidermotropic CD8-positive T-cell lymphoma
visual_anchor: Rapid ulcerated papules, plaques, and tumors, sometimes with mucosal involvement.
rationale: Distinct cutaneous lymphoma, but ulcerated plaques and tumors alone do not establish separate visual value beyond existing cutaneous T cell lymphoma coverage.
source_heading: Primary cutaneous aggressive epidermotropic CD8-positive T-cell lymphoma
final_name: Primary cutaneous aggressive epidermotropic CD8-positive T-cell lymphoma

canonical_name: Indolent T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder of the gastrointestinal tract
visual_anchor: Superficial small-bowel ulcers, small polyps, and villous flattening without bulky mass.
rationale: The proposed endoscopic or cross-sectional appearance is nonspecific and does not provide enough independent visual teaching value for a separate atlas entry.
source_heading: Indolent T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder of the gastrointestinal tract
final_name: Indolent T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder of the gastrointestinal tract

visual_anchor: Vesiculopustular lesions in a neonate with Down syndrome, sometimes concentrated at adhesive or venipuncture sites; blood evaluation establishes transient abnormal myelopoiesis.
rationale: Visible neonatal eruption with linked hematologic context.

visual_anchor: Generalized cervical/axillary lymphadenopathy with splenomegaly on examination or ultrasound/CT.
rationale: Distinct immune dysregulation syndrome with conspicuous lymphoproliferation, though imaging is not syndrome-specific.

visual_anchor: Chest radiograph may show absent thymic shadow; characteristic costochondral flaring/cupping (“scorbutic”/rachitic-like) is supportive but not universal.
rationale: Distinctive ADA deficiency can have skeletal manifestations; avoid claiming the radiograph alone separates all SCID forms.

visual_anchor: Congenital alopecia with eyebrow/lash loss and nail dystrophy on clinical photographs; absent thymic shadow on infant radiograph.
rationale: Characteristic visible ectodermal phenotype distinguishes FOXN1 deficiency among SCID causes.

visual_anchor: Chronic necrotizing skin ulcers and nasal cartilage destruction; bronchiectasis may be seen on chest CT.
rationale: Distinct visible granulomatous phenotype of MHC-I deficiency (bare lymphocyte syndrome type I).

visual_anchor: Extensive recalcitrant cutaneous warts; bone marrow smear shows hypermature neutrophils with nuclear hypersegmentation/filamentous chromatin.
rationale: The combination is highly teachable, but marrow morphology is needed to anchor myelokathexis.

visual_anchor: Deep dermatophytosis with plaques/nodules or draining abscesses; MRI can show Candida brain abscess.
rationale: Distinct fungal susceptibility with dermatologic and radiologic images.

visual_anchor: Oral ulcers/periodontitis and marrow promyelocyte maturation arrest.
rationale: Recognizable clinical photo and confirmatory marrow image; separate congenital neutropenia entity.

visual_anchor: Howell–Jolly bodies on peripheral smear; ultrasound/CT confirms absent spleen with situs solitus.
rationale: Distinct morphologic blood-film and anatomic imaging anchor for congenital absence of spleen.

visual_anchor: Infantile perianal fistulas/abscesses and deep colonic ulcers on endoscopy.
rationale: Visually distinctive early-onset enterocolitis/skin disease linked to IL-10 pathway defects.

visual_anchor: Provocation images: linear wheal after stroking, wheal after cold/heat/pressure/light/water exposure, or pinpoint post-exercise wheals.
rationale: Broaden the existing urticaria topic to include chronic inducible subtypes, trigger-specific wheals, and standardized provocation tests; keep those as subsections within the existing disease page.

visual_anchor: PLAID can show evaporative cold urticaria and neonatal acral ulcers; APLAID more often has blistering or inflammatory skin lesions without cold induced symptoms.
rationale: Visible and trigger-linked manifestations support a distinct inherited immune dysregulation topic.

visual_anchor: Spine radiographs show platyspondyly/metaphyseal lesions; brain CT can show basal-ganglia calcification.
rationale: Distinct skeletal-neurologic imaging syndrome and immune phenotype.

visual_anchor: Brittle woolly hair with trichorrhexis nodosa on light microscopy, plus characteristic facial appearance.
rationale: A strong clinical phenotype provides a visual anchor for this syndromic immunodeficiency.

visual_anchor: Brain MRI shows corpus-callosum agenesis, colpocephaly, and pontine/cerebellar hypoplasia; hypopigmentation/cataracts clinically.
rationale: Distinct syndromic neuroimaging plus visible phenotype supports a separate topic.

visual_anchor: CT shows gas in renal parenchyma/collecting system with possible perinephric extension.
rationale: Life-threatening infection with a distinctive imaging emergency, separate from xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis.

visual_anchor: CTA or catheter angiogram shows multifocal mid/distal renal-artery beading.
rationale: Distinct nonatherosclerotic renovascular disease versus ostial plaque stenosis.

visual_anchor: CT/urography shows fused lower poles via midline isthmus, low position, and anteriorly rotated renal pelves.
rationale: Common congenital fusion anomaly with recognizable cross-sectional anatomy.

visual_anchor: Both renal moieties lie on one side; trace the crossed ureter to its normal contralateral bladder insertion on CT/urography.
rationale: Distinct congenital positional anomaly; ureter tracking resolves a mass/missing-kidney mimic.

visual_anchor: CT urography in excretory phase shows contrast-filled papillary clefts (ball-on-tee/golf-ball-on-tee), ring signs, or sloughed papilla.
rationale: Renal papillary necrosis is not a new standalone atlas topic under the existing catalog policy; expand the renal manifestations in the existing sickle-cell disease topic with a dedicated imaging sign only if the site supports focused manifestations.

visual_anchor: Contrast CT shows bilateral cortical hypoenhancement with preserved medullary enhancement (reverse-rim sign); chronic cortical calcification may follow.
rationale: Distinct diffuse ischemic injury from renal infarction; correct anchor is reverse-rim, not cortical-rim sign.

visual_anchor: Subcapsular hematoma compresses/flattenes renal parenchyma on CT or ultrasound, with new secondary hypertension.
rationale: Imageable post-traumatic/iatrogenic compressive nephropathy.

visual_anchor: Left renal vein compression with a beak and gonadal or pelvic collaterals on Doppler or CT, paired with compatible hematuria or pain; distinguish asymptomatic compression.
rationale: Distinct symptomatic venous-compression syndrome; a close cross-specialty analogue but a separate vascular territory.

visual_anchor: Multiple bilateral renal cysts in small echogenic kidneys on ultrasound/CT in advanced CKD or dialysis.
rationale: Acquired dialysis-associated cyst disease distinct from inherited enlarged-kidney ADPKD.

visual_anchor: Bilateral enlarged echogenic kidneys on ultrasound in advanced untreated HIV; microcystic tubular changes are biopsy based.
rationale: Collapsing glomerulopathy in HIV is already within the focal segmental glomerulosclerosis spectrum; enlarged echogenic kidneys are nonspecific. Add the HIV associated clinical and imaging context to that page.

canonical_name: Renal osteodystrophy (CKD mineral and bone disorder)
visual_anchor: Hand films may show subperiosteal phalangeal resorption; spine may show rugger-jersey endplates, with vascular/soft-tissue calcification.
rationale: Clinically useful constellation of CKD bone/mineral disease, not a single pathognomonic sign.
source_heading: Renal osteodystrophy (CKD mineral and bone disorder)

visual_anchor: CT shows tethered, clustered small bowel, peritoneal thickening/calcification, and obstruction (“abdominal cocoon”).
rationale: This duplicates the separately proposed GI encapsulating peritoneal sclerosis topic. Keep as ADD here for central deduplication; the eventual one disease page should include long-term peritoneal dialysis as a cause/context.

visual_anchor: Potential image set spans aneurysmal fistula, steal ischemia, central-vein stenosis, and access duplex findings.
rationale: Umbrella title combines distinct complications and fails single-disease topic grain; defer or split into independently scoped vascular-access syndromes.

visual_anchor: MRI shows innumerable tiny bilateral cortical and medullary T2-bright microcysts in chronic lithium exposure.
rationale: Distinctive drug-associated imaging phenotype.

visual_anchor: Medullary nephrocalcinosis on US/CT; pediatric rickets films may show metaphyseal cupping/fraying.
rationale: A visual complication pattern can complement acid-base diagnosis; avoid conflation with medullary sponge kidney.

visual_anchor: Clinical images of swollen muscle/dark urine and possible MRI muscle edema; urine dipstick blood without RBCs is not itself a visual disease anchor.
rationale: Muscle edema is nonspecific and the defining diagnosis is laboratory based; current image anchor is weak for a standalone atlas page.

visual_anchor: Contrast CT may show wedge-shaped hypoenhancement or a striated nephrogram; lobar nephronia appears mass-like.
rationale: Acute pyelonephritis has a well-developed imaging pattern and is not an existing index topic; include lobar nephronia as a focal variant within the same page.

visual_anchor: Round or wedge-shaped low-attenuation renal/perinephric collection with enhancing rim on contrast CT.
rationale: Distinct suppurative focus with a clear drainage-relevant imaging finding.

visual_anchor: Obstructed collecting system with mobile echogenic debris/fluid-debris level on ultrasound, with hydronephrosis.
rationale: Urgent infected obstruction with characteristic sonographic debris and need for drainage.

visual_anchor: DMSA shows polar cortical scars; CT/urography shows clubbed calyces beneath scars.
rationale: Existing vesicoureteral reflux topic covers the causal disease; represent reflux nephropathy as a manifestation/complication under that page.

visual_anchor: Small/normal echogenic kidneys with corticomedullary-junction cysts on ultrasound.
rationale: Prototype inherited tubulointerstitial nephropathy with an imageable, if nonspecific, pattern.

visual_anchor: Renal ultrasound shows cysts/dysplasia; abdominal imaging may show hypoplastic or absent pancreatic body/tail.
rationale: Multisystem pattern is recognizable and distinct from isolated cystic kidney disease.

visual_anchor: Bilateral medullary nephrocalcinosis in a neonate with antenatal polyhydramnios.
rationale: Nephrocalcinosis offers an image anchor for an otherwise biochemical tubulopathy; share imaging with differential, not as a unique sign.

visual_anchor: Renal calculi or medullary nephrocalcinosis on CT/US after malabsorption or bowel surgery.
rationale: Distinct acquired metabolic cause, but stones and nephrocalcinosis are nonspecific. Teach malabsorption associated hyperoxaluria in stone and nephrocalcinosis differentials.

visual_anchor: Multiple bilateral homogeneous hypoenhancing renal masses, diffuse enlargement, or perirenal rind on CT/MRI.
rationale: Distinct infiltrative renal malignancy pattern versus a typical solitary hypervascular RCC.

visual_anchor: Infiltrative hypoenhancing central/medullary renal mass in a young patient, often with sickle cell trait and nodal disease.
rationale: Distinct aggressive medullary tumor with high-value clinical context and imaging pattern.

visual_anchor: CTA shows long smooth narrowing of abdominal aorta, often with renal-artery ostial stenoses.
rationale: Distinct abdominal aortic/renal artery narrowing pattern. This duplicates a proposal from another specialty and is left ADD for central cross-specialty deduplication.

visual_anchor: Small cortical renal mass on CT/MRI in a patient with severe renin-mediated hypertension and hypokalemia.
rationale: Reninoma is distinct, but the proposed small cortical mass is nonspecific and the useful discriminator is biochemical renin excess.

visual_anchor: Nephrocalcinosis/rickets can occur but are nonspecific; diagnosis relies on low-molecular-weight proteinuria and genetics.
rationale: No disease-specific clinical/radiologic finding is offered, and existing primary hyperoxaluria/renal mineral topics cover the imaging phenotype.

visual_anchor: White pearly mass medial to an intact tympanic membrane; non-echo-planar diffusion restriction on MRI.
rationale: Congenital cholesteatoma is a congenital form/site subtype of the existing cholesteatoma topic. Add a clearly labeled congenital subsection to avoid a duplicate page while retaining the pearl-like mass behind an intact tympanic membrane and diffusion-restriction findings.

visual_anchor: Central tympanic-membrane perforation with mucopurulent drainage and inflamed middle-ear mucosa on otoscopy.
rationale: Chronic suppurative otitis media is already represented in the existing tympanic_membrane_perforation topic by chronic drainage. Expand that page with the central perforation, purulent otorrhea, and chronic infection findings.

visual_anchor: Discrete chalk-white plaques in the tympanic membrane, often with reduced membrane mobility.
rationale: A recognizable otoscopic finding separate from acute effusion or perforation.

visual_anchor: Dense keratin plug filling an expanded external canal, with severe otalgia and conductive hearing loss.
rationale: Distinctive canal lesion, visually separate from focal canal cholesteatoma.

visual_anchor: Focal canal-floor soft-tissue erosion with sequestrated bone on temporal-bone CT; keratin debris on otoscopy.
rationale: Distinct from middle-ear cholesteatoma; the destructive canal location is the image anchor.

visual_anchor: Single dense pedunculated bony projection from the external auditory canal on otoscopy/CT.
rationale: Separate from usually multiple broad-based cold-water exostoses.

visual_anchor: Small pit immediately anterior to the ascending helix; expressible discharge when infected.
rationale: Classic external clinical appearance with congenital tract distinction.

visual_anchor: Canal plane temporal bone CT shows a superior canal roof defect, paired with compatible sound or pressure induced symptoms and physiologic findings.
rationale: High-value third-window disorder with a distinct diagnostic CT plane; avoid CT-alone diagnosis.

visual_anchor: Enlarged vestibular aqueduct on high-resolution temporal-bone CT, measured at midpoint; commonly bilateral.
rationale: Distinct congenital inner-ear imaging abnormality; not equivalent to Pendred syndrome.

canonical_name: Cholesterol granuloma of the petrous apex
visual_anchor: Petrous-apex lesion with high signal on both T1- and T2-weighted MRI and smooth expansion.
rationale: Distinctive MRI signal pattern separates it from petrous-apex effusion and cholesteatoma.
source_heading: Cholesterol granuloma of the petrous apex
final_name: Cholesterol granuloma of the petrous apex

visual_anchor: Petrous-apex opacification/erosion on temporal-bone CT with adjacent apical inflammation; diplopia from CN VI palsy.
rationale: Clinically important skull-base infection with an anatomic imaging correlate.

canonical_name: Nasal foreign body, including a button battery
visual_anchor: Unilateral nasal discharge with visible foreign body; button battery may produce septal ulceration/perforation.
rationale: Common pediatric emergency and distinct from esophageal foreign body.
source_heading: Nasal foreign body, including a button battery
final_name: Nasal foreign body, including a button battery

visual_anchor: Boggy, fluctuant bilateral septal swelling obstructing both nasal passages after trauma.
rationale: A time-sensitive finding recognized by direct examination; distinct from septal abscess.

visual_anchor: Well-defined ivory-density lesion attached to a frontal or ethmoid sinus wall on CT.
rationale: Typical benign sinonasal bone tumor with a crisp CT anchor.

visual_anchor: Single opacified sinus containing central hyperattenuating/calcific material with reactive wall sclerosis on CT.
rationale: Characteristic noninvasive fungal-ball pattern, distinct from allergic fungal disease and invasive fungal infection.

visual_anchor: Unilateral infiltrative sinonasal soft tissue with bone destruction and extrasinus extension on CT/MRI.
rationale: Distinct chronic invasive form, but overlap with acute invasive fungal disease warrants precise scope.

visual_anchor: Unilateral maxillary sinus opacification contiguous with a diseased maxillary tooth or dental implant on CT.
rationale: A useful imaging-defined source of unilateral sinus disease; separate from primary rhinosinusitis.

visual_anchor: Smooth cystic swelling at the nasal ala/vestibule, typically below the piriform aperture on CT/MRI.
rationale: Distinct extraosseous cyst with visible nasal-facial contour change.

visual_anchor: Intranasal mass continuous with intracranial contents through a skull-base defect; CSF signal on MRI.
rationale: Basal intranasal meningoencephalocele is an anatomic subtype of the existing encephalocele topic. Add the intranasal/skull-base presentation and CSF-signal MRI findings as a focused site section.

visual_anchor: Newborn with bluish medial-canthal swelling and contiguous intranasal cyst at the inferior meatus on endoscopy/imaging.
rationale: Congenital dacryocystocele is covered by the existing dacryocystitis and nasolacrimal duct obstruction topic, which already includes lacrimal sac mucocele/NLDO. Add the newborn medial-canthal mass and intranasal cyst as a congenital subsection.

visual_anchor: Midline septal, turbinate, and palatal ulceration with cartilage/bone destruction; palate perforation in advanced disease.
rationale: Distinct destructive clinical pattern; retain as separate exposure-related mimic of GPA and malignancy.

visual_anchor: Irregular enhancing sinonasal mass with focal bone destruction and orbital/skull-base extension on CT/MRI.
rationale: Common sinonasal primary malignancy not covered by listed pharyngeal/laryngeal carcinoma entities.

visual_anchor: Bilateral symmetric callus-like lesions at the junction of anterior and middle thirds of true vocal folds on laryngoscopy.
rationale: Classic symmetric phonotrauma lesion distinguishable from a unilateral polyp.

visual_anchor: Unilateral focal pedunculated or sessile lesion on the free edge of a true vocal fold.
rationale: Distinct focal lesion from bilateral nodules or diffuse Reinke edema.

visual_anchor: Bilateral diffuse gelatinous/polypoid swelling of the true vocal folds on laryngoscopy.
rationale: Distinct diffuse bilateral lesion with characteristic endoscopic appearance.

visual_anchor: Posterior vocal-process granuloma at the arytenoid vocal process on laryngoscopy.
rationale: Site-specific lesion separate from membranous-fold polyp or cyst.

visual_anchor: Smooth subepithelial vocal-fold cyst causing focal bulge and impaired mucosal wave on stroboscopy.
rationale: Distinct subepithelial lesion with imageable endoscopic/stroboscopic finding.

visual_anchor: Short circumferential fibrotic narrowing immediately below the glottis on endoscopy/CT.
rationale: High-value fixed airway lesion; separate from vasculitic stenosis within GPA.

visual_anchor: Thin anterior glottic web visible at laryngoscopy, sometimes with a small anterior notch.
rationale: Distinct congenital airway morphology with direct endoscopic teaching value.

visual_anchor: Posterior interarytenoid cleft on direct laryngoscopy/bronchoscopy; aspiration on swallow study.
rationale: Distinct congenital aspiration/airway lesion with procedural and imaging correlate.

visual_anchor: Smooth cyst arising in vallecula, displacing epiglottis posteriorly on flexible laryngoscopy.
rationale: Recognizable congenital supraglottic lesion with potential neonatal airway compromise.

visual_anchor: Unilateral expiratory air trapping/hyperinflation on chest film; foreign body seen on bronchoscopy.
rationale: Classic pediatric airway foreign-body pattern and clinically urgent.

visual_anchor: Dynamic expiratory collapse of the tracheal lumen on bronchoscopy or dynamic CT.
rationale: Distinct dynamic airway disorder rather than fixed stenosis.

visual_anchor: Hypervascular carotid bifurcation mass splaying ICA and ECA (lyre sign) on CTA/MRA.
rationale: Distinct paraganglioma site and signature vascular displacement pattern.

visual_anchor: Periauricular pit/cyst or draining sinus with tract through/parotid region toward external auditory canal.
rationale: Distinct first-arch anomaly from the listed second-arch lateral-neck cyst.

canonical_name: Pyriform sinus fistula (third or fourth branchial anomaly)
visual_anchor: Left pyriform sinus tract to thyroid/perithyroid region with inflammatory change or recurrent suppurative thyroiditis.
rationale: The existing branchial cleft cyst and sinus topic already includes pyriform-sinus third/fourth-arch tracts. Expand it with left-sided tract anatomy and recurrent suppurative thyroiditis.
source_heading: Pyriform sinus fistula (third or fourth branchial anomaly)
final_name: Pyriform sinus fistula (third or fourth branchial anomaly)

visual_anchor: Rim-enhancing collection in parapharyngeal space on contrast CT, with airway displacement.
rationale: Distinct deep-neck-space infection; retain separate from peritonsillar and retropharyngeal abscess.

visual_anchor: Unilateral tender swollen salivary gland with purulent drainage at duct orifice.
rationale: Direct clinical image plus ductal purulence distinguishes bacterial infection from stones/mumps.

visual_anchor: Displaced or comminuted nasal-bone fracture on facial CT, with bridge deviation/swelling clinically.
rationale: Common facial fracture with recognizable external deformity; many isolated cases are clinical diagnoses.

visual_anchor: CT shows zygomatic arch depression, widened lateral orbit, and disruption of zygomaticomaxillary/orbital rims.
rationale: Common midface fracture complex with teachable CT pattern.

visual_anchor: Orbital floor defect with herniated orbital fat/inferior rectus and maxillary hemosinus on coronal CT.
rationale: High-value trauma pattern with entrapment relevance.

canonical_name: Le Fort fractures (types I–III as one topic)
visual_anchor: CT shows Le Fort fracture line crossing the maxilla/pterygoid plates; classify I, II, or III by separation level.
rationale: Essential midface trauma classification with clear CT anatomy.
source_heading: Le Fort fractures (types I–III as one topic)
final_name: Le Fort fractures (types I–III as one topic)
