visual_anchor: Mandibular cortical discontinuity on panoramic radiograph/CT; assess symphysis, body, angle, and condyle.
rationale: Common facial fracture with clinically relevant site pattern.

canonical_name: Temporal bone fracture (otic-capsule sparing versus violating)
visual_anchor: High-resolution temporal-bone CT shows fracture line and whether it crosses otic capsule; associated hemotympanum/CSF leak.
rationale: Distinct fracture classification predicts important inner-ear and facial-nerve injury.
source_heading: Temporal bone fracture (otic-capsule sparing versus violating)
final_name: Temporal bone fracture (otic-capsule sparing versus violating)

visual_anchor: CT cartilage discontinuity or laryngeal framework displacement with laryngoscopic mucosal injury/airway edema.
rationale: Potentially life-threatening airway trauma with complementary radiologic and endoscopic findings.

visual_anchor: Territorial diffusion restriction, early CT ischemic changes, and arterial occlusion on CTA.
rationale: Core emergency with management relevant imaging.

visual_anchor: Blood in basal cisterns and sulci on CT, with a causative aneurysm on CTA or angiography.
rationale: Distinct hemorrhagic emergency from intraparenchymal hemorrhage.

visual_anchor: Rim enhancing epidural collection with cord or cauda equina compression on MRI.
rationale: Distinct imageable spinal infection requiring urgent recognition.

visual_anchor: Anterior cord diffusion restriction; sagittal pencil like signal and axial owl eyes may occur.
rationale: Named vascular cord disease; signs are supportive rather than uniquely diagnostic.

visual_anchor: MRI demonstrates the compressive cause; clinical saddle sensory and sphincter findings define the emergency.
rationale: Add emergency presentation and red flags to lumbar disc herniation and stenosis pages, with cross links to tumors and infection.

visual_anchor: Facial diplegia or flaccid weakness; smooth cauda equina root enhancement can support an atypical case.
rationale: Core clinical syndrome; enhancement is nonspecific and MRI is not a routine confirmatory test.

visual_anchor: Symmetric central pontine signal with peripheral sparing, sometimes with extrapontine lesions.
rationale: Recognizable toxic metabolic MRI pattern.

visual_anchor: Bilateral globus pallidus injury and delayed white matter abnormalities may appear on MRI.
rationale: Important toxic exposure with a memorable imaging differential; normal early imaging does not exclude it.

visual_anchor: Susceptibility blooming coating cerebellar folia, brainstem, and cranial nerves.
rationale: Distinct distribution and chronic clinical syndrome; separate from cortical siderosis in cerebral amyloid angiopathy.

visual_anchor: Alternating concentric rings on T2 and diffusion imaging.
rationale: Distinctive concentric demyelinating lesion pattern; overlap with multiple sclerosis does not mean every case is established MS.

visual_anchor: Numerous punctate and curvilinear enhancing foci centered on the pons and cerebellar peduncles.
rationale: Recognizable inflammatory syndrome; label as a diagnosis requiring exclusion of mimics, especially lymphoma.

visual_anchor: Corpus callosum swelling or injury with selective central layer involvement.
rationale: Distinct alcohol or malnutrition associated callosal disease.

visual_anchor: Symmetric dentate nucleus abnormalities, sometimes involving the splenium or brainstem.
rationale: Characteristic medication associated imaging pattern.

visual_anchor: Curvilinear DWI hyperintensity along the corticomedullary junction.
rationale: Strong imaging clue beyond the confirmatory skin biopsy; not present in every case.

canonical_name: Biotin thiamine responsive basal ganglia disease
visual_anchor: Symmetric caudate and putamen swelling or injury on MRI in acute encephalopathy.
rationale: Treatable metabolic disorder with an important imaging trigger; genetic confirmation is needed.
final_name: Biotin thiamine responsive basal ganglia disease

canonical_name: HTRA1 related cerebral small vessel disease
visual_anchor: Leukoencephalopathy with lacunes; classic CARASIL adds early alopecia and spondylosis, and an arc sign can involve the pons and middle cerebellar peduncles.
rationale: Distinct from CADASIL; use HTRA1 spectrum title and CARASIL as a searchable phenotype.
final_name: HTRA1 related cerebral small vessel disease

visual_anchor: Bilateral thalamic lesions, sometimes involving basal ganglia and brainstem.
rationale: Imageable neuroinfection; pattern requires epidemiologic and laboratory context.

visual_anchor: Brainstem and cerebellar peduncle inflammation or microabscesses on MRI.
rationale: Distinctive hindbrain distribution makes a useful neuroinfection topic.

visual_anchor: Longitudinal gray matter predominant spinal cord T2 signal with acute asymmetric flaccid weakness.
rationale: Important pediatric syndrome distinct from poliomyelitis.

visual_anchor: Progressive white matter abnormalities and atrophy are nonspecific; EEG and virologic evidence establish the syndrome.
rationale: A distinct delayed measles associated CNS disease, not an acute measles subtype; proposed MRI is nonspecific and key EEG or serologic findings are outside the clinical and radiologic image focus. Cross link from measles if expanded later.

visual_anchor: Bilateral pallidal signal abnormalities, with chronic T2 changes; early bilirubin injury can be T1 bright.
rationale: Core neonatal toxic brain injury; state sequence and disease stage correctly.

canonical_name: Germinal matrix and intraventricular hemorrhage of prematurity
visual_anchor: Caudothalamic groove hemorrhage and intraventricular blood on cranial ultrasound.
rationale: Distinct neonatal hemorrhage pattern; include periventricular hemorrhagic infarction as an associated venous injury.
final_name: Germinal matrix and intraventricular hemorrhage of prematurity

visual_anchor: Periventricular cysts or white matter volume loss with irregular ventricular margins.
rationale: Classic injury of prematurity, distinct from term neonatal hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy.

visual_anchor: Excess small gyri with an irregular cortical surface and gray white junction on MRI.
rationale: Imaging defined cortical malformation; keep regional forms together.

visual_anchor: Gray matter signal nodules lining the lateral ventricles.
rationale: Distinct migration disorder from subcortical band heterotopia.

visual_anchor: Intraventricular or spinal mass; posterior fossa tumors may extend through the fourth ventricular outlets.
rationale: Major missing neurooncology topic; organize by current molecular and anatomic classification, not an assertion that every type is the same tumor.

visual_anchor: Cortical or subcortical infiltrative mass often containing calcification.
rationale: Important brain tumor differential; imaging cannot establish IDH mutation or 1p19q codeletion.

visual_anchor: Superficial cortical tumor, often temporal, sometimes cystic with a mural nodule or calcification.
rationale: Distinct epilepsy associated glioneuronal tumor; separate from DNET.

visual_anchor: Bubbly multinodular cortical lesion with little mass effect in a patient with epilepsy.
rationale: Separate tumor with a useful MRI pattern; do not combine with ganglioglioma.

visual_anchor: Scapular winging with patchy muscle denervation edema or atrophy on MRI.
rationale: Recognizable clinical and imaging syndrome, distinct from entrapment neuropathy.

visual_anchor: Frontal and anterior temporal predominant atrophy or hypometabolism.
rationale: Major dementia syndrome with imageable regional patterns; keep phenotypes within one topic.

visual_anchor: Symmetric cerebellar and posterior cerebral white matter abnormalities.
rationale: Characteristic exposure related distribution; preserve common chasing the dragon search term.

visual_anchor: Symmetric dorsal column cord signal may mimic vitamin B12 related subacute combined degeneration.
rationale: Teach as an etiologic differential in the existing dorsal column syndrome page; no independent visual discriminator is supplied.

visual_anchor: Dorsal column inverted V signal from functional vitamin B12 inactivation.
rationale: Add exposure specific cause and clinical teaching to existing subacute combined degeneration.

visual_anchor: Confluent white matter injury, callosal thinning, persistent diffusion abnormalities, and small CT calcifications.
rationale: Distinct adult white matter disorder; use current spectrum name and retain ALSP as a search alias.
source_heading: Adult-onset leukoencephalopathy with axonal spheroids (CSF1R / ALSP)

visual_anchor: Cystic bone lesions paired with frontal predominant white matter degeneration.
rationale: Distinct combined skeletal and neurologic syndrome.

canonical_name: Retinal vasculopathy with cerebral leukoencephalopathy and systemic manifestations
visual_anchor: Retinal vascular abnormalities and enhancing white matter lesions that can resemble tumors.
rationale: Multisystem TREX1 associated syndrome; separate from Aicardi Goutieres syndrome.
final_name: Retinal vasculopathy with cerebral leukoencephalopathy and systemic manifestations

visual_anchor: Iron sensitive substantia nigra and pallidal signal, with a T1 bright nigral halo in later disease.
rationale: Distinct NBIA phenotype with strong MRI teaching value.

visual_anchor: Posterior cortical and thalamic MRI abnormalities with refractory epilepsy and liver disease.
rationale: Recognizable POLG related clinicoradiologic phenotype; findings are not specific alone.

visual_anchor: Symmetric thalamic lesions, sometimes with concentric hemorrhagic or necrotic components.
rationale: Distinct infection triggered encephalopathy rather than infectious encephalitis itself.

visual_anchor: Deep gray, brainstem, or anterior horn abnormalities can accompany encephalitis or acute flaccid paralysis.
rationale: Useful neuroinfectious differential; MRI may be normal and laboratory confirmation is essential.

visual_anchor: Dorsal brainstem signal with a compatible hand foot and mouth eruption.
rationale: Distinct neuroinvasive syndrome with a recognizable posterior brainstem pattern; cross link to hand foot and mouth disease rather than equating the two.

visual_anchor: Diffuse edema and meningeal enhancement lack a reliable distinguishing imaging pattern.
rationale: The proposal relies on organism microscopy and late nonspecific necrosis, insufficient for the current clinical and radiologic scope.

visual_anchor: Focal or diffuse thickened enhancing dura on MRI.
rationale: Thickened enhancing dura is nonspecific, and the idiopathic label is exclusionary. Prioritize etiology defined or more distinctive clinicoradiologic topics.

visual_anchor: Radial perivascular enhancement extending from the ventricles, with possible cord or meningeal involvement.
rationale: Distinct autoimmune syndrome from genetic GFAP associated Alexander disease; imaging is supportive.

visual_anchor: Multifocal infarct like lesions of different ages or other variable brain MRI abnormalities.
rationale: Existing Hematology topic already names the same disease; expand neurologic coverage.

visual_anchor: Cerebral hemiatrophy with ipsilateral calvarial thickening and sinus enlargement.
rationale: Coherent clinicoradiologic syndrome with a memorable structural pattern.

visual_anchor: Porencephaly, small vessel disease, and variable ocular abnormalities such as cataract.
rationale: Distinct genetic multisystem disease spectrum; avoid separate pages for every manifestation.

visual_anchor: Near absence of cerebral hemispheres replaced by fluid, with preserved falx and variable deep structures.
rationale: Distinct severe malformation from hydrocephalus and holoprosencephaly.

canonical_name: Horizontal gaze palsy with progressive scoliosis
visual_anchor: Split pons and butterfly shaped medulla with progressive scoliosis.
rationale: Distinct structural brainstem and skeletal syndrome.
source_heading: Horizontal gaze palsy with progressive scoliosis
final_name: Horizontal gaze palsy with progressive scoliosis

visual_anchor: Fusion of cerebellar hemispheres across a deficient vermis.
rationale: Imaging defined hindbrain malformation; syndromic associations belong within the topic.

visual_anchor: Small ventral pons and cerebellum; a dragonfly configuration occurs in some forms.
rationale: Use a single clinicoradiologic family topic with genetic subtypes; no claim that the dragonfly pattern occurs in all forms.

visual_anchor: Congenital weakness or contractures with extensive characteristic white matter signal abnormalities.
rationale: Distinct muscle and brain phenotype, not covered by Walker Warburg or Ullrich disease.

visual_anchor: Focal ventral cord displacement and kinking through a dural defect on MRI.
rationale: Distinct structural cause of progressive myelopathy.

visual_anchor: Focal dorsal cord indentation producing a sagittal scalpel sign, sometimes with a syrinx.
rationale: Specific structural lesion; distinguish from ventral cord herniation and arachnoid cyst.

visual_anchor: Extra axial CSF like lesion with marked DWI hyperintensity.
rationale: Distinct intracranial developmental lesion from cutaneous epidermal inclusion cyst.

visual_anchor: Fat containing intracranial lesion, with disseminated fat droplets after rupture.
rationale: Distinct developmental lesion with a strong CT and MRI anchor.

visual_anchor: Bubbly intraventricular mass near the foramen of Monro and septum pellucidum.
rationale: Useful age and location based tumor pattern.

visual_anchor: Frond like avidly enhancing ventricular papilloma versus invasive heterogeneous carcinoma with necrosis or dissemination; hydrocephalus may accompany either.
rationale: Distinct ventricular tumor from ependymoma; imaging alone does not establish benignity.

visual_anchor: Superficial hemispheric cyst and mural nodule, sometimes with meningeal contact.
rationale: Named cortical tumor with useful age, epilepsy, and location context.

visual_anchor: Thin corpus callosum and ears of the lynx white matter signal near the frontal horns.
rationale: Distinct MRI supported spastic paraplegia; sign also occurs in SPG15 and is not uniquely diagnostic.

visual_anchor: Calf pseudohypertrophy and muscle fatty replacement overlap Duchenne disease.
rationale: Broaden existing Duchenne page to dystrophinopathies and show Becker comparison; a separate near identical visual page adds little.

visual_anchor: Miyoshi phenotype shows prominent posterior calf wasting, with selective muscle involvement on imaging.
rationale: Use a single DYSF spectrum topic including Miyoshi and limb girdle presentations.

visual_anchor: Long myopathic face, ptosis, ophthalmoparesis, and severe neonatal hypotonia.
rationale: Visible phenotype supports a clinical atlas entry beyond its biopsy finding.

visual_anchor: Hypotonia is nonspecific; central cores are a muscle histology finding.
rationale: No sufficiently distinctive clinical or radiologic anchor is supplied.

canonical_name: Hereditary neuropathy with liability to pressure palsies
visual_anchor: Recurrent focal palsies have no stable distinctive photograph; tomacula require nerve histology.
rationale: Primarily electrodiagnostic and genetic diagnosis with weak standalone visual value.
source_heading: Hereditary neuropathy with liability to pressure palsies
final_name: Hereditary neuropathy with liability to pressure palsies

visual_anchor: Asymmetric hand wasting and nerve enlargement are nonspecific.
rationale: Prioritize stronger phenotype and image based additions; diagnosis depends on electrophysiology and clinical context.

visual_anchor: PAS positive sweat gland inclusions are histologic.
rationale: The proposed teaching image is pathology rather than a clinical or radiologic manifestation.

visual_anchor: Ragged red fibers are histologic and multiple lipomas are variable and nonspecific.
rationale: Insufficient independent clinical or radiologic anchor for current release.

visual_anchor: Cerebellar atrophy alone is nonspecific; pallidal iron may appear later.
rationale: Defer the proposed infantile phenotype until a distinct reproducible clinical and MRI image set is demonstrated.

visual_anchor: Smooth tongue from absent fungiform papillae and absent overflow emotional tears.
rationale: Directly photographable diagnostic phenotype distinct from congenital insensitivity to pain with anhidrosis.

visual_anchor: Central interphalangeal erosions with gull wing or saw tooth configuration.
rationale: Add an erosive phenotype section to existing osteoarthritis; new imaging content does not require a new disease page.

visual_anchor: Digital clubbing with symmetric long bone periostosis and parallel cortical scintigraphic uptake.
rationale: Useful acquired syndrome across multiple causes; distinct from primary pachydermoperiostosis.
source_heading: Secondary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy (Pierre-Marie-Bamberger syndrome, hypertrophic pulmonary osteoarthropathy)

visual_anchor: Joint fragmentation, debris, disorganization, and collapse; rocker bottom foot in advanced midfoot disease.
rationale: Coherent image defined syndrome across etiologies; keep all joints and causes together.

visual_anchor: Diffuse femoral head and neck marrow edema, later osteopenia, without the typical focal necrotic boundary.
rationale: Important clinical and imaging differential from osteonecrosis and insufficiency fracture.
source_heading: Transient osteoporosis of the hip, including regional migratory osteoporosis

visual_anchor: Periarticular bone cysts and destructive spondyloarthropathy after long term dialysis.
rationale: Distinct precursor protein and distribution from systemic AL amyloidosis.

visual_anchor: Rapidly progressive woody palmar thickening with flexion contractures and polyarthritis.
rationale: Distinct photographable paraneoplastic syndrome; retain underlying malignancy associations in the page.

visual_anchor: Painless lateral proximal interphalangeal soft tissue thickening without erosions.
rationale: Useful visible mimic of inflammatory arthritis.

canonical_name: Camptodactyly arthropathy coxa vara pericarditis syndrome
visual_anchor: Camptodactyly, noninflammatory joint swelling, and coxa vara with short femoral necks.
rationale: Distinct PRG4 associated clinical and skeletal phenotype.
final_name: Camptodactyly arthropathy coxa vara pericarditis syndrome

visual_anchor: Carpal and tarsal osteolysis with palmoplantar nodules and contractures.
rationale: Canonical MMP2 related MONA topic; Torg and NAO belong here, while MMP14 Winchester syndrome is separate.
source_heading: Multicentric osteolysis, nodulosis, and arthropathy (MONA, Torg, Winchester, NAO; MMP2 or MMP14, one topic)

visual_anchor: Progressive osteolysis and contractures overlap MONA.
rationale: Keep separate in disease ontology; defer a second closely overlapping visual page until its own useful clinical and imaging set is demonstrated.
source_heading: Multicentric osteolysis, nodulosis, and arthropathy (MONA, Torg, Winchester, NAO; MMP2 or MMP14, one topic)

visual_anchor: Childhood diffuse lung disease with ground glass, cysts, and nodules paired with arthritis.
rationale: Distinct inherited immune dysregulation syndrome; place in Immunology with rheumatology and pulmonology cross links.

visual_anchor: Early aortic or valve calcification, abnormal dentition, and acro osteolysis.
rationale: Strong multisystem radiographic phenotype.

visual_anchor: Indurated bound down skin with hypertrichosis and joint contractures.
rationale: Directly visible fibrosing disorder distinct from stiff person syndrome and systemic sclerosis.

visual_anchor: Periarticular cutaneous nodules with rapidly developing flexion contractures.
rationale: Recognizable clinicocutaneous syndrome; biopsy supports diagnosis.

visual_anchor: Irregular bulky periosteal new bone, often involving ribs, clavicles, or scapulae.
rationale: Distinct medication associated radiographic phenotype from smoother secondary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy.

visual_anchor: Cranial ultrasound shows echogenic clot at the caudothalamic groove with grade-dependent ventricular filling, dilation, or periventricular hemorrhagic infarction.
rationale: High-frequency neonatal ultrasound diagnosis with a grading scheme and serial visual evolution; not a parent already in the catalog.
final_name: Germinal matrix and intraventricular hemorrhage of prematurity

visual_anchor: Cranial ultrasound/MRI shows periventricular echogenicity evolving to bilateral posterior periventricular cysts or white-matter volume loss.
rationale: Distinct pediatric presentation with a recognizable clinical or imaging pattern and no equivalent topic in the live catalog.

visual_anchor: MRI shows symmetric T1 hyperintensity of globus pallidus/subthalamic nuclei; chronic disease may show T2 signal and movement disorder.
rationale: Distinct pediatric presentation with a recognizable clinical or imaging pattern and no equivalent topic in the live catalog.

visual_anchor: Diffuse boggy scalp collection crosses sutures and midline, with subaponeurotic fluid on ultrasound; unlike suture-confined cephalohematoma.
rationale: A high-stakes neonatal scalp finding with strong clinical and ultrasound distinction from existing cephalohematoma.

canonical_name: Physical Child Abuse: Skeletal and Intracranial Imaging
visual_anchor: Classic metaphyseal lesions, suspicious rib fracture patterns, and intracranial injury; interpret the entire clinical context rather than treating an isolated sign as proof.
rationale: A core recognition topic with high-specificity radiographic injury patterns and clear clinical importance.

visual_anchor: Expiratory/decubitus chest radiograph shows persistent unilateral hyperlucency/air trapping and sometimes contralateral mediastinal shift despite a radiolucent object.
rationale: Distinct pediatric presentation with a recognizable clinical or imaging pattern and no equivalent topic in the live catalog.

visual_anchor: Neonatal radiograph shows dilated small-bowel loops with little or no distal gas and contrast enema reveals unused microcolon; apple-peel variant has a spiral distal bowel around a single vascular pedicle.
rationale: Distinct neonatal obstruction pattern, including the visually memorable apple-peel vascular anatomy; duodenal atresia is a different level and already listed.

visual_anchor: Contrast enema shows a normal-caliber colon with long filling defect from meconium; plug may evacuate during the study.
rationale: Separate imaging diagnosis from existing meconium ileus and Hirschsprung disease, with a recognizable contrast-enema target.
source_heading: Meconium plug syndrome and small left colon syndrome

visual_anchor: Contrast enema shows a small descending/sigmoid colon with abrupt caliber transition at the splenic flexure and a normal-caliber rectum.
rationale: A distinct functional neonatal obstruction pattern with a useful contrast-enema sign.
source_heading: Meconium plug syndrome and small left colon syndrome

visual_anchor: Ultrasound shows a cyst contiguous with bowel and a layered gut-signature wall (echogenic mucosa over hypoechoic muscle), sometimes a Y sign.
rationale: Distinct pediatric presentation with a recognizable clinical or imaging pattern and no equivalent topic in the live catalog.

visual_anchor: Cross-sectional imaging reveals abnormal organ laterality, interrupted IVC with azygos continuation or anomalous venous return, splenic anomalies, and complex congenital heart anatomy.
rationale: A clinically important multisystem laterality pattern with highly teachable cross-sectional anatomy; comparator Kartagener syndrome is a different disorder.
source_heading: Heterotaxy syndrome (situs ambiguous, asplenia or polysplenia)

visual_anchor: Well newborn has blanching erythematous macules/papules with central papules or pustules, mainly trunk and proximal limbs, sparing palms and soles.
rationale: Common one-look benign newborn eruption with practical clinical photo differential; distinct from transient neonatal pustular melanosis.

visual_anchor: A constricting hair or thread with distal swelling or ischemia on a digit, toe, or penis; include genital presentations within one topic.
rationale: Distinct pediatric presentation with a recognizable clinical or imaging pattern and no equivalent topic in the live catalog.

visual_anchor: Coarse facial gestalt, temporal alopecia, pigmentary mosaicism, and hypotonia; mosaic tetrasomy 12p may be missed in blood.
rationale: Distinct face/skin pattern supports visual clinical recognition; mosaicism explains variable phenotype.

visual_anchor: Wide mouth with full lips, deep-set eyes, broad nasal bridge, and characteristic intermittent hyperventilation/apnea in a child with severe developmental delay.
rationale: Distinct facial and episodic breathing phenotype extends the dysmorphology differential alongside separately listed Angelman and Mowat-Wilson syndromes.

visual_anchor: Coronal craniosynostosis with variable hypertelorism, brachydactyly/carpal-tarsal fusion, and hearing loss; CT demonstrates the fused coronal suture.
rationale: A common molecularly defined syndromic craniosynostosis with a recognizable clinical and CT phenotype; other listed craniosynostosis syndromes are distinct.

visual_anchor: Severe symmetric tetraphocomelia or limb reduction with cleft lip/palate, microcephaly, and characteristic facial dysmorphism.
rationale: Distinct limb-reduction and craniofacial pattern; the thalidomide phenotype is an etiologic phenocopy rather than the same disease.

visual_anchor: Postaxial limb-ray deficiency with malar hypoplasia, micrognathia, and cup-shaped ears.
rationale: Distinct postaxial acrofacial pattern; contrasts with the already listed preaxial Nager syndrome.

visual_anchor: Coarse facial appearance, distal nail hypoplasia, and diaphragmatic hernia on prenatal or neonatal imaging.
rationale: Syndromic pattern adds recognizable dysmorphology and nail clues to an existing diaphragmatic hernia topic.

visual_anchor: Prenatal valproate exposure may produce characteristic facial features, metopic ridge, radial-ray defects, and neural-tube defects.
rationale: Etiology-specific teratogenic pattern with visible craniofacial and limb findings; distinct exposure from fetal hydantoin/warfarin syndromes.

visual_anchor: Nasal hypoplasia with stippled epiphyses/vertebrae on skeletal radiographs after first-trimester exposure.
rationale: Distinct radiographic and facial teratogenic pattern; different exposure mechanism from other embryopathies.

visual_anchor: Lateral sacral radiograph shows hemisacrum/sickle-shaped sacrum; MRI/US depicts presacral mass with anorectal malformation.
rationale: Classic triad and recognizable sacral sign distinguish this syndrome from broader caudal regression/sacral agenesis.

visual_anchor: Prenatal/neonatal imaging shows aqueductal stenosis with hydrocephalus; examination shows adducted thumbs.
rationale: Recognizable neurologic and limb combination with a specific neuroimaging anchor.

visual_anchor: Strictly unilateral, sharply demarcated ichthyosiform inflammatory nevus follows Blaschko lines with ipsilateral limb hypoplasia/reduction.
rationale: High-value one-look lateralized skin and limb pattern with disease-specific distribution.

visual_anchor: Radial-styloid pain with positive Finkelstein/Eichhoff maneuver; US shows thickened first dorsal compartment tendon sheath.
rationale: Distinct radiographic or clinical pattern supports an independent orthopedic atlas topic.

visual_anchor: Ulnar-distribution paresthesia and intrinsic hand weakness; ultrasound/MRI shows enlarged ulnar nerve at cubital tunnel, sometimes with dynamic subluxation.
rationale: Distinct radiographic or clinical pattern supports an independent orthopedic atlas topic.

visual_anchor: Merge with osteoarthritis; first MTP joint-space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, and dorsal osteophyte with reduced dorsiflexion.
rationale: Degenerative first-MTP arthropathy fits the existing osteoarthritis topic; add the dorsal osteophyte/limited-dorsiflexion pattern there.

visual_anchor: Inspection shows fixed or flexible hammertoe (PIP flexion), mallet toe (DIP flexion), or claw toe (MTP hyperextension with IP flexion); weight-bearing film defines alignment.
rationale: Distinct radiographic or clinical pattern supports an independent orthopedic atlas topic.

visual_anchor: Forefoot squeeze/Mulder click; US/MRI shows plantar interdigital nerve thickening in a web space, classically third-fourth.
rationale: Distinct radiographic or clinical pattern supports an independent orthopedic atlas topic.

visual_anchor: Lateral heel film shows posterosuperior calcaneal prominence with retrocalcaneal bursal fluid and distal Achilles insertional thickening.
rationale: Distinct radiographic or clinical pattern supports an independent orthopedic atlas topic.

visual_anchor: Dynamic US during resisted eversion shows peroneal tendons snapping anterior to fibula due to superior retinaculum injury; MRI depicts retinaculum tear.
rationale: Distinct radiographic or clinical pattern supports an independent orthopedic atlas topic.

visual_anchor: MRI shows diffuse femoral-head/neck marrow edema and effusion without serpiginous necrotic line or subchondral collapse.
rationale: Distinct radiographic or clinical pattern supports an independent orthopedic atlas topic.

canonical_name: Subchondral insufficiency fracture of the knee
visual_anchor: MRI shows subchondral low-signal fracture line with extensive marrow edema, usually medial femoral condyle; early radiographs may be normal.
rationale: Distinct radiographic or clinical pattern supports an independent orthopedic atlas topic.

visual_anchor: After spinal cord/brain injury, radiograph/CT shows periarticular ectopic bone bridging soft tissues, commonly around hip.
rationale: Distinct radiographic or clinical pattern supports an independent orthopedic atlas topic.

visual_anchor: MRI shows focal cervical disc extrusion/protrusion indenting ventral thecal sac or compressing a nerve root/spinal cord.
rationale: Distinct radiographic or clinical pattern supports an independent orthopedic atlas topic.

visual_anchor: CT shows posterior ligamentum flavum ossification, often thoracic; MRI demonstrates posterior canal narrowing and cord compression.
rationale: Distinct radiographic or clinical pattern supports an independent orthopedic atlas topic.

visual_anchor: MRI shows a fluid-signal juxtafacet cyst communicating with degenerative lumbar facet and narrowing lateral recess/canal.
rationale: Distinct radiographic or clinical pattern supports an independent orthopedic atlas topic.

visual_anchor: Lateral lumbar radiograph/CT shows close contact and sclerosis of adjacent spinous processes; MRI may show interspinous bursitis/edema.
rationale: Distinct radiographic or clinical pattern supports an independent orthopedic atlas topic.

visual_anchor: Acute severe shoulder pain followed by patchy weakness/atrophy; MR neurography may show focal nerve signal or denervation edema, but no specific image sign.
rationale: Clinical pain-then-weakness pattern is important, but imaging is often normal or nonspecific and does not justify a visual atlas entry.

visual_anchor: AP leg radiograph shows partial/complete tibial absence or hypoplasia with fibular bowing and knee/ankle deformity.
rationale: Distinct radiographic or clinical pattern supports an independent orthopedic atlas topic.

visual_anchor: Forearm/hand radiographs show hypoplastic or absent ulna with radial bowing and ulnar-sided digit deficiency.
rationale: Distinct radiographic or clinical pattern supports an independent orthopedic atlas topic.

visual_anchor: Forearm radiograph shows proximal radius-ulna bony bridge with fixed pronation; distinguish from syndromic synostosis.
rationale: Distinct radiographic or clinical pattern supports an independent orthopedic atlas topic.

visual_anchor: Clinical/radiographic central ray deficiency creates median cleft with absent central metacarpals/metatarsals and divergent digits.
rationale: Distinct radiographic or clinical pattern supports an independent orthopedic atlas topic.

visual_anchor: Newborn knee rests in hyperextension; lateral radiograph/US shows anterior tibial displacement relative to distal femur.
rationale: Distinct radiographic or clinical pattern supports an independent orthopedic atlas topic.

visual_anchor: Visible painless midclavicular prominence; radiograph shows a gap/nonunion, usually right midshaft, with tapered ends.
rationale: Distinct radiographic or clinical pattern supports an independent orthopedic atlas topic.

visual_anchor: Skeletal survey shows metaphyseal widening, irregularity, cupping/fraying and severe short-limb disproportion.
rationale: Distinct radiographic or clinical pattern supports an independent orthopedic atlas topic.

visual_anchor: Radiographs show marked metaphyseal expansion of long bones with thin cortices (Erlenmeyer-flask shape), especially around knees.
rationale: Distinct radiographic or clinical pattern supports an independent orthopedic atlas topic.

visual_anchor: Radiographs show long-bone metaphyseal flaring/sclerosis and modeling defects; skull films show supraorbital hyperostosis and craniofacial changes.
rationale: Distinct radiographic or clinical pattern supports an independent orthopedic atlas topic.

visual_anchor: CT distinguishes Tillaux fracture of the anterolateral distal tibial epiphysis from triplane fracture involving epiphysis, physis, and metaphysis in three planes.
rationale: Combine the two adolescent transitional patterns under one physis-crossing ankle-fracture topic, with subtype-specific CT anatomy.

visual_anchor: US/MRI shows distended olecranon or prepatellar bursa with thick hyperemic wall, echogenic debris, and surrounding cellulitis.
rationale: The olecranon and prepatellar sites are one infection pattern; teach as a single septic bursitis topic.

visual_anchor: Pediatric forearm radiographs show torus cortical buckling or greenstick fracture with one cortex broken and the opposite cortex bowed/intact.
rationale: Torus and greenstick injuries are paired pediatric incomplete-fracture patterns and should share one page.

visual_anchor: Basal subpleural fibrosis for asbestosis; pleural plaques, diffuse pleural thickening, and associated rounded atelectasis as distinct nonmalignant manifestations.
rationale: Strong exposure-linked fibrosis pattern. Keep distinct findings as a unified asbestos-related thoracic disease topic with pleural plaque and rounded-atelectasis subsections.

visual_anchor: Basal subpleural fibrosis for asbestosis; pleural plaques, diffuse pleural thickening, and associated rounded atelectasis as distinct nonmalignant manifestations.
rationale: Highly imageable exposure effect, best grouped with asbestosis and rounded atelectasis in one asbestos-related thoracic disease topic.

visual_anchor: Pleural-based rounded mass adjacent to thickened pleura, with converging bronchovascular structures curving into the lesion (comet-tail sign).
rationale: Memorable mass mimic in asbestos-related pleural disease; include as a subsection in unified asbestos-related thoracic disease page.

visual_anchor: V/Q scan shows segmental mismatched perfusion defects; CTPA shows eccentric organized thrombus, webs/bands, pouch defects, mosaic perfusion, and enlarged bronchial arteries.
rationale: Distinct chronic organized vascular disease from acute PE, with treatable pulmonary hypertension and diagnostic imaging criteria.

visual_anchor: HRCT may show peripheral ground-glass opacity or consolidation; high-attenuation lung opacities and high-attenuation liver/spleen support iodine-rich drug accumulation.
rationale: Distinct medication-associated lung injury pattern with a potentially useful attenuation clue.

visual_anchor: CT after intravenous injection of talc containing crushed tablets may show centrilobular micronodules, high attenuation deposits, and later fibrosis or emphysema.
rationale: Distinct particulate exposure with memorable distribution and vascular/centrilobular imaging; separate from silicosis and coal pneumoconiosis.

visual_anchor: After long-bone injury, conjunctival/axillary petechiae; chest CT may show diffuse or patchy ground-glass opacity, septal thickening, and centrilobular nodules.
rationale: Time-sensitive trauma syndrome with a characteristic clinical petechial distribution plus pulmonary imaging findings.

visual_anchor: HRCT shows lower-lung-predominant ground-glass opacity or fine reticulation with relative subpleural sparing; traction bronchiectasis if fibrotic.
rationale: Subpleural sparing is a useful imaging pattern distinguishing NSIP from UIP, though secondary causes must be considered.

canonical_name: Alveolar Macrophage Pneumonia (formerly Desquamative Interstitial Pneumonia)
visual_anchor: HRCT typically shows diffuse/basal ground-glass opacity in a smoker, sometimes with subpleural sparing and emphysema.
rationale: Use current ERS/ATS 2025 term “alveolar macrophage pneumonia” (AMP); preserve DIP as a former-name synonym. Radiology and smoking context support a visual topic.
final_name: Alveolar Macrophage Pneumonia (formerly Desquamative Interstitial Pneumonia)

visual_anchor: HRCT shows upper-lobe centrilobular/paraseptal emphysema with lower-lobe subpleural fibrosis/honeycombing in the same patient.
rationale: Distinct mixed pattern with physiologic consequences and radiographic contrast across lung zones.

visual_anchor: Expiratory HRCT shows patchy lobular air trapping/mosaic attenuation, sometimes with bronchiectasis and bronchial-wall thickening.
rationale: Distinct small-airway disease and bilateral counterpart to the unilateral postinfectious Swyer–James pattern.

canonical_name: Diffuse Idiopathic Pulmonary Neuroendocrine Cell Hyperplasia (DIPNECH)
visual_anchor: HRCT shows diffuse mosaic attenuation/air trapping with multiple small centrilobular nodules and occasional tumorlets or carcinoids.
rationale: Distinct airway-neuroendocrine disorder with a recognizable combined CT pattern.
source_heading: Diffuse idiopathic pulmonary neuroendocrine cell hyperplasia (DIPNECH)
final_name: Diffuse Idiopathic Pulmonary Neuroendocrine Cell Hyperplasia (DIPNECH)

visual_anchor: Unilateral air trapping/hyperinflation or atelectasis on expiratory chest radiograph; object may be directly visualized at bronchoscopy.
rationale: Common, actionable pediatric airway emergency with clinical and endoscopic teaching value.

visual_anchor: Contrast CT shows loculated lenticular pleural fluid with enhancing visceral and parietal pleura (split-pleura sign); necessitans extends through chest wall.
rationale: Broaden existing thoracic empyema necessitans page to Pleural Empyema (including necessitans), preserving the existing sign and representing extension as a complication.

visual_anchor: Inspiratory/expiratory CT shows peripheral cystic bronchiectasis from deficient cartilaginous support in fourth- to sixth-order bronchi, with dynamic ballooning/collapse.
rationale: Rare congenital bronchiectasis phenotype; imageable but the classic description is based on limited cases.

visual_anchor: CT shows a blind-ending bronchus with a mucocele/bronchocele and adjacent segmental hyperinflation/air trapping.
rationale: Characteristic paired mucocele plus hyperinflation is highly teachable and distinct from other congenital lung malformations.

visual_anchor: Smooth, sharply marginated water-attenuation mediastinal (often subcarinal) or intrapulmonary cyst on CT; proteinaceous contents may increase attenuation.
rationale: Distinct foregut-derived mediastinal lesion and useful cystic-mass differential.

visual_anchor: CTA shows left pulmonary artery arising from right pulmonary artery and passing between trachea and esophagus, often with airway compression.
rationale: Distinct vascular-airway congenital anomaly with actionable cross-sectional anatomy.

visual_anchor: Axial CT/bronchoscopy shows a circular O-shaped trachea lacking the posterior membranous wall, often with long-segment stenosis.
rationale: Distinct congenital airway morphology; may accompany pulmonary artery sling but should remain an independently describable anomaly.

visual_anchor: HRCT shows geographic ground-glass opacity concentrated in the right middle lobe, lingula, and paramediastinal lung, with air trapping/hyperinflation.
rationale: Distinct infant diffuse-lung-disease pattern; diagnosis requires clinical context and careful exclusion of alternatives.

visual_anchor: Pediatric CT shows a unilateral multicystic or mixed solid-cystic lung mass; solid type may invade pleura/chest wall.
rationale: High-stakes pediatric malignancy and key differential for CPAM; separate organ-specific neoplasm.

visual_anchor: CT shows one or more peripheral, often slowly growing calcified nodules; cysts may coexist.
rationale: Broaden the existing localized tracheobronchial amyloidosis topic to localized pulmonary amyloidosis and add the nodular form; preserve different radiologic distributions within that disease.

visual_anchor: CT shows a well-circumscribed or lobulated anterior mediastinal soft-tissue mass; pleural “drop” implants can indicate dissemination.
rationale: A common anterior mediastinal tumor with distinct thoracic anatomy and staging pattern.

visual_anchor: Anterior mediastinal mass with macroscopic fat, fluid, soft tissue, and coarse calcification/teeth; fat-fluid level may be present.
rationale: Highly recognizable imaging pattern of a mature mediastinal germ-cell tumor; retain distinct thoracic site from ovarian/testicular teratomas.

visual_anchor: Smoker with ill-defined upper-lobe centrilobular nodules, patchy ground-glass opacity, bronchial-wall thickening, and often emphysema on HRCT.
rationale: A distinct symptomatic smoking-related ILD with an imageable pattern, although it overlaps smoking-related macrophage disorders.

canonical_name: Hard-Metal Lung Disease (Giant Cell Interstitial Pneumonia)
visual_anchor: Occupational CT may show ground-glass opacity, centrilobular nodules, mosaic attenuation/air trapping, and fibrosis with traction bronchiectasis.
rationale: The supplied clinical or imaging appearance is nonspecific; the defining exposure, histology, or hemodynamic result does not provide a strong independent visual teaching pattern.
source_heading: Hard-Metal Lung Disease (Giant Cell Interstitial Pneumonia)
final_name: Hard-Metal Lung Disease (Giant Cell Interstitial Pneumonia)

visual_anchor: Chest CT commonly shows bilateral ground-glass opacity with subpleural/lobular sparing, sometimes consolidation or upper-lobe centrilobular nodules.
rationale: Current exposure-linked acute lung injury with a recognizable but nonspecific imaging spectrum; preserve exposure-based diagnostic framing.

visual_anchor: CT shows upper-lobe-predominant centrilobular ground-glass nodules or calcified nodules in chronic renal failure/hyperparathyroidism; bone scintigraphy may show diffuse pulmonary uptake.
rationale: A radiologically distinctive metabolic complication that is separate from primary alveolar microlithiasis.

visual_anchor: Dense fine pulmonary nodules after iron, tin, or barium dust exposure; keep siderosis, stannosis, and baritosis as labeled etiologic sections.
rationale: One of three named inert-metal pneumoconioses; keep separate candidate records, but they may be presented together in an inert-metal pneumoconiosis section because clinical effects and imaging patterns overlap.

visual_anchor: Diffuse ground glass, septal thickening, and variable cystic change in term neonates or children; label SFTPB, SFTPC, ABCA3, and NKX2-1 subtypes and do not infer genotype from CT.
rationale: One pediatric diffuse lung disease topic with genetic subtypes; do not publish separate near identical scan galleries for each surfactant gene.

visual_anchor: Absent or rudimentary ipsilateral main bronchus with absent lung tissue and vasculature, ipsilateral volume loss, and compensatory contralateral expansion.
rationale: Distinct congenital absence of lung, bronchus, and vessels; differentiate from aplasia and prior pneumonectomy.

visual_anchor: Absent or rudimentary ipsilateral main bronchus with absent lung tissue and vasculature, ipsilateral volume loss, and compensatory contralateral expansion.
rationale: Distinct from agenesis by rudimentary blind bronchus; retain as separate congenital anomaly.

canonical_name: Proximal Interruption of a Pulmonary Artery
visual_anchor: CT angiography shows absent proximal branch pulmonary artery with distal intrapulmonary branches supplied by systemic collaterals and a small ipsilateral lung.
rationale: Distinct congenital vascular anomaly and cause of hemoptysis; not equivalent to scimitar syndrome.
source_heading: Proximal Interruption of a Pulmonary Artery
final_name: Proximal Interruption of a Pulmonary Artery

visual_anchor: CTA/MRA shows focal pulmonary-vein narrowing or abrupt cutoff with regional septal thickening, ground-glass edema, waxing/waning opacities, or decreased perfusion.
rationale: Distinct venous obstruction and important mimic of infection or pulmonary embolism; congenital and acquired forms can be explained together.

visual_anchor: CTPA shows a lobulated, expansile filling defect with vessel enlargement/wall-eclipsing; MRI shows heterogeneous enhancement and PET may be FDG avid.
rationale: Rare but critical PE mimic with a distinct tumor-like vascular imaging pattern.

visual_anchor: Dynamic expiratory CT or bronchoscopy demonstrates excessive expiratory collapse of the trachea and/or main bronchi.
rationale: Distinct dynamic central-airway disorder; separate from tracheal diverticula/bronchiectasis in Mounier–Kuhn syndrome.

visual_anchor: Endoscopy/CT shows a short concentric scar-like narrowing below the glottis, commonly in the cricoid/subglottic airway.
rationale: Duplicate cross-specialty candidate with Otolaryngology; leave ADD for central deduplication into one airway page.

visual_anchor: CT shows smooth submucosal tracheal or main-bronchial wall thickening/narrowing, sometimes with longitudinal extension; bronchoscopy shows a submucosal lesion.
rationale: A tracheobronchial salivary-gland-type primary has a characteristic airway-centered appearance and is clinically distinct from conventional lung carcinoma and salivary-gland ACC; the existing broad primary lung carcinoma topic excludes subtype proliferation, so a focused airway topic is justified.

visual_anchor: Central endobronchial soft-tissue nodule/mass on CT causing focal airway narrowing, atelectasis, or recurrent postobstructive infection.
rationale: Distinct bronchial primary with airway-specific presentation; do not merge with oral/salivary mucoepidermoid carcinoma solely for shared histology.

visual_anchor: CT shows a solitary, well-circumscribed, often peripheral lung nodule/mass with variable enhancement or calcification.
rationale: The supplied clinical or imaging appearance is nonspecific; the defining exposure, histology, or hemodynamic result does not provide a strong independent visual teaching pattern.

visual_anchor: Usually a well-circumscribed, peripherally located, round/oval nodule with homogeneous enhancement; marginal pseudocapsule or overlying-vessel sign may appear.
rationale: Distinct lung neoplasm with useful solitary-nodule image, not a generic “sclerosing” tumor subtype.

visual_anchor: Well-circumscribed paravertebral/posterior mediastinal mass, often with smooth neural-foraminal widening or dumbbell extension on CT/MRI.
rationale: Thoracic anatomic location provides distinct imaging differential; do not merge solely with vestibular schwannoma.

visual_anchor: Smooth elevated intact hemidiaphragm with preserved continuity on CT/ultrasound; dynamic ultrasound can show reduced excursion.
rationale: Distinct from diaphragmatic hernia because the diaphragm remains intact; clear radiographic/dynamic anchor.

visual_anchor: Chest radiograph/CT shows mediastinal air outlining the heart, great vessels, or trachea, sometimes with continuous-diaphragm sign.
rationale: Distinct from pneumothorax and tension pneumothorax; clinical context distinguishes spontaneous from traumatic/iatrogenic causes.

visual_anchor: Neonatal imaging may show diffuse interstitial thickening, septal lines, ground-glass opacity, and pleural effusions; pathology demonstrates dilated lymphatics.
rationale: The supplied clinical or imaging appearance is nonspecific; the defining exposure, histology, or hemodynamic result does not provide a strong independent visual teaching pattern.

canonical_name: Alveolar Capillary Dysplasia with Misalignment of Pulmonary Veins (ACD/MPV)
visual_anchor: Neonate with refractory pulmonary hypertension and diffuse bilateral opacities; imaging is nonspecific.
rationale: Pathology-led lethal developmental disorder without a disease-specific clinical or radiologic visual anchor; defer under current scope.
source_heading: Alveolar Capillary Dysplasia with Misalignment of Pulmonary Veins (ACD/MPV)
final_name: Alveolar capillary dysplasia with misalignment of pulmonary veins

visual_anchor: CT may show multiple cysts and nodules, often peribronchovascular, with airway-wall thickening or calcification.
rationale: Distinct parenchymal/airway deposition disorder from systemic AL amyloidosis and tracheobronchial amyloidosis; radiologic pattern merits separate topic.

visual_anchor: Thin branching, bone-density opacities in dependent lower-lobe subpleural/interstitial lung on CT, often incidentally detected.
rationale: Distinct branching ossification pattern and useful radiologic teaching entity.

visual_anchor: Bronchoscopy shows black anthracotic pigmentation with bronchial narrowing/stenosis, often involving the right middle lobe; CT may show calcified nodes and atelectasis.
rationale: Highly recognizable bronchoscopic appearance with useful TB/exposure context.

visual_anchor: Multiple left pleural-based nodules on CT after remote splenic trauma/splenectomy; lesions enhance like splenic tissue and show uptake on heat-damaged RBC scan.
rationale: Distinct benign thoracic nodule mimic with a specific history and confirmatory nuclear medicine study.

visual_anchor: CT may show enlarged main pulmonary artery, right-heart enlargement, and peripheral vascular pruning; imaging supports but does not establish PAH.
rationale: The supplied clinical or imaging appearance is nonspecific; the defining exposure, histology, or hemodynamic result does not provide a strong independent visual teaching pattern.

visual_anchor: Imaging may show multifocal ground-glass opacity or consolidation resembling organizing pneumonia or diffuse alveolar damage.
rationale: Primarily a histopathologic pattern with no specific radiologic signature; parent instruction recommends deferring absent stronger visual value.

visual_anchor: CT findings can include centrilobular nodules, tree-in-bud opacities, septal thickening, and pulmonary artery enlargement, all nonspecific.
rationale: Severe but usually diagnosed pathologically or postmortem; no reliable disease-specific visual anchor for a standalone atlas topic.

visual_anchor: After aspiration of kerosene/fire-breathing fuel, CT may show fat-attenuation consolidation or crazy-paving with dependent distribution.
rationale: Named exposure syndrome is a form of exogenous lipoid pneumonia; merge into existing exogenous_lipoid_pneumonia and preserve “fire-eater” as context/synonym.

visual_anchor: Acute exposure may cause nonspecific bilateral opacities, delayed pulmonary edema, or bronchiolitis obliterans.
rationale: Toxic exposure syndrome with nonspecific radiology and no reliably distinctive photograph; defer per focused visual-atlas criteria.

visual_anchor: Focal or diffuse pancreatic enlargement overlaps type 1 autoimmune pancreatitis and pancreatic carcinoma.
rationale: Distinct IgG4 unrelated disease, but no reliable separate clinical or radiologic discriminator is supplied; do not equate it with IgG4 related disease.
